name: Aabraham
desc: Finnish form of Abraham.

name: Aada
desc: Finnish form of Ada 1.

name: Aadan
desc: Possibly a Somali form of Adam.

name: Aadolf
desc: Finnish form of Adolf.

name: Aafje
desc: Short form of names beginning with the Old German element alb "elf".

name: Aage
desc: Danish and Norwegian form of Áki.

name: Aali
desc: Means "high, lofty, sublime" in Arabic.

name: Aalis
desc: Old French form of Alice.

name: Aaliyah
desc: Feminine form of Aali. It was popularized in the English-speaking world by the singer Aaliyah Haughton (1979-2001), who was known simply as Aaliyah. This name received a boost in popularity after she released her debut album in 1994, and also in 2001 after her untimely death in an airplane crash.

name: Aamadu
desc: Fula form of Ahmad.

name: Aamina
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic آمنة (see Aminah 1), as well as the Somali form.

name: Aaminah
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic آمنة (see Aminah 1).

name: Aaminata
desc: Fula form of Aminah 1.

name: 'Aamir
desc: Means "prosperous, substantial" in Arabic.

name: Aamir 1
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عامر (see 'Aamir), as well as the usual Urdu transcription.

name: Aamir 2
desc: Variant of Amir 1.

name: Aamu
desc: Means "morning" in Finnish.

name: Aanakwad
desc: Means "cloud" in Ojibwe.

name: Aang
desc: The hero of the American animated television series Avatar: The Last Airbender (2005-2008). When his name is shown in written form, it is composed of the Chinese characters 安 (ān) meaning "peace, quiet" and 昂 (áng) meaning "raise, lift".

name: Aapeli
desc: Finnish form of Abel.

name: Aapo
desc: Finnish form of Abraham.

name: Aaralyn
desc: Feminine elaboration of Aaron using the popular name suffix lyn.

name: Aaren
desc: Variant or feminine form of Aaron.

name: Aarne
desc: Finnish and Estonian form of Arne 1.

name: Aarni
desc: Finnish form of Arne 1, also associated with the archaic word aarni meaning "treasure".

name: Aaro
desc: Finnish and Estonian form of Aaron.

name: Aäron
desc: Dutch form of Aaron.

name: Aarón
desc: Spanish form of Aaron.

name: Aaron
usage: English, French, German, Finnish, Jewish, Biblical, Biblical Latin, Biblical Greek
desc: From the Hebrew name אַהֲרֹן ('Aharon), which is most likely of unknown Egyptian origin. Other theories claim a Hebrew derivation, and suggest meanings such as "high mountain" or "exalted". In the Old Testament this name is borne by the older brother of Moses. He acted as a spokesman for his brother when they appealed to the pharaoh to release the Israelites from slavery. Aaron's rod produced miracles and plagues to intimidate the pharaoh. After the departure from Egypt and arrival at Mount Sinai, God installed Aaron as the first high priest of the Israelites and promised that his descendants would form the priesthood.... [more]

name: Aarre
desc: Means "treasure" in Finnish. It may also be used as a variant of the uncommon older name Aaretti, itself from a Low German form of Arnold.

name: Aart
desc: Dutch short form of Arnold.

name: Aarthi
desc: Tamil form of Aarti.

name: Aarti
desc: From the name of a Hindu ritual in which offerings of lamps or candles are made to various gods, derived from Sanskrit आरात्रिक (aratrika).

name: Aase
desc: Danish form of Åsa.

name: Aatami
desc: Finnish form of Adam.

name: Aatos
desc: Means "thought" in Finnish.

name: Aatto
desc: Finnish form of Adolf. It also means "eve, evening before" in Finnish, as the day before an important holiday.

name: Aatu
desc: Finnish form of Adolf.

name: Aava
desc: Means "wide, open" in Finnish.

name: Abacuc
desc: Biblical Latin form of Habakkuk.

name: Abaddon
desc: Means "ruin, destruction" in Hebrew. In Revelation in the New Testament this is another name of the angel of the abyss.

name: Abbán
desc: Means "little abbot", derived from Irish abb "abbot" combined with a diminutive suffix. This was the name of a 6th-century Irish saint, the son of King Cormac of Leinster.

name: 'Abbas
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic/Persian عبّاس (see Abbas).

name: Abbas
desc: Means "austere" in Arabic. This was the name of the Prophet Muhammad's uncle. It was also borne by a son of Ali, the fourth caliph.

name: Abbe
desc: Variant of Abe 2.

name: Abbey
desc: Diminutive of Abigail.

name: Abbi
desc: Diminutive of Abigail.

name: Abbie
desc: Diminutive of Abigail.

name: Abbondio
desc: Italian form of Abundius.

name: Abby
desc: Diminutive of Abigail.

name: Abd al-Aziz
desc: Means "servant of the powerful" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with عزيز ('aziz) meaning "powerful". This was the name of the first king of modern Saudi Arabia.

name: Abd al-Hamid
desc: Means "servant of the praiseworthy" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with حَمِيد (hamid) meaning "praiseworthy". This was the name of two sultans of the Ottoman Empire.

name: Abd al-Haqq
desc: Means "servant of the truth" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with حقّ (haqq) meaning "truth".

name: Abd al-Kader
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد القادر (see Abd al-Qadir).

name: Abd al-Karim
desc: Means "servant of the generous" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with كَرِيم (karim) meaning "generous".

name: Abd Allah
desc: Means "servant of Allah" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with الله (Allah). This was the name of the Prophet Muhammad's father. He died before his son's birth.

name: Abd al-Latif
desc: Means "servant of the gentle" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with لطيف (latif) meaning "gentle".

name: Abd al-Majid
desc: Means "servant of the glorious" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with مجيد (majid) meaning "glorious".

name: Abd al-Malik
desc: Means "servant of the king" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with ملك (malik) meaning "king". This was the name of the fifth Umayyad caliph, who made Arabic the official language of the empire.

name: Abd al-Qadir
desc: Means "servant of the capable, servant of the powerful" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with قادر (qadir) meaning "capable, powerful". This was the name of a 19th-century Algerian resistance leader.

name: Abd al-Rahim
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحيم (see Abd ar-Rahim).

name: Abd al-Rahman
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحمٰن (see Abd ar-Rahman).

name: Abd al-Rashid
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرشيد (see Abd ar-Rashid).

name: Abd al-Salam
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد السلام (see Abd as-Salam).

name: Abd al-Wali
desc: Means "servant of the guardian" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with ولِي (wali) meaning "guardian, friend".

name: Abd ar-Rahim
desc: Means "servant of the merciful" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with رحيم (rahim) meaning "merciful".

name: Abd ar-Rahman
desc: Means "servant of the merciful" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with رحمن (rahman) meaning "merciful". This was the name of two early caliphs of the Umayyad dynasty in Spain.

name: Abd ar-Rashid
desc: Means "servant of the rightly guided" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with رَشِيد (rashid) meaning "rightly guided".

name: Abd as-Salam
desc: Means "servant of the peaceful" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with سلام (salam) meaning "peace".

name: Abdastartos
desc: Greek form of Abdastartus.

name: Abdastartus
desc: From the Greek form Ἀβδάσταρτος (Abdastartos) of the Phoenician name 𐤏𐤁𐤃𐤏𐤔𐤕𐤓𐤕 (ʿAbdʿashtart) meaning "servant of Ashtoreth", derived from 𐤏𐤁𐤃 (ʿabd) meaning "servant, slave" combined with the name of the goddess Ashtoreth. This was the name of a 10th-century BC king of Tyre, as recorded by the historian Josephus.

name: Abdelaziz
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد العزيز (see Abd al-Aziz) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdelhak
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الحقّ (see Abd al-Haqq) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdelhamid
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الحميد (see Abd al-Hamid) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdelkader
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد القادر (see Abd al-Qadir) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdellatif
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد اللطيف (see Abd al-Latif) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdelmajid
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد المجيد (see Abd al-Majid) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abderrahim
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحيم (see Abd ar-Rahim) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abderrahmane
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحمٰن (see Abd ar-Rahman) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdeslam
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد السلام (see Abd as-Salam) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdessalam
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد السلام (see Abd as-Salam) chiefly used in Northern Africa.

name: Abdias
desc: Form of Obadiah used in the Greek and Latin Old Testament, as well as the Portuguese form (used chiefly in Brazil).

name: Abdiel
desc: Means "servant of God" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament, this is the name of a member of the tribe of Gad. In John Milton's Paradise Lost (1667), this is the name of a seraph who withstands Satan when he urges the angels to revolt.

name: Abdiou
desc: Form of Obadiah used in the Greek Old Testament, also spelled Ἀβδίας (Abdias).

name: Abdolhossein
desc: Means "servant of al-Husayn" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with حسّین (Hosseyn), the Persian form of Arabic Husayn. This name refers to Husayn ibn Ali, the son of Ali.

name: Abdollah
desc: Persian form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdolreza
desc: Means "servant of al-Ridha" from Arabic عبد ('abd) meaning "servant" combined with رضا (Reza), the Persian form of Arabic Ridha. This name refers to the 9th-century Shia imam Ali al-Ridha.

name: Abdou
desc: Form of Abduh common in western and northern Africa.

name: Abdoul
desc: Form of Abdul used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Abdoulaye
desc: Form of Abd Allah used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Abduh
desc: Means "his servant" in Arabic.

name: Abdul
usage: Arabic, Urdu, Punjabi, Pashto, Uzbek, Bengali, Indonesian, Malay
desc: First part of compound Arabic names beginning with عبد ال ('Abd al) meaning "servant of the" (such as عبد العزيز ('Abd al-'Aziz) meaning "servant of the powerful").

name: Abdulah
desc: Bosnian form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdülaziz
desc: Turkish form of Abd al-Aziz.

name: Abdul Aziz
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد العزيز (see Abd al-Aziz).

name: Abdulaziz
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد العزيز (see Abd al-Aziz).

name: Abdul Hamid
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الحميد (see Abd al-Hamid).

name: Abdülhamit
desc: Turkish form of Abd al-Hamid.

name: Abdul Haq
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الحقّ (see Abd al-Haqq), as well as the usual Urdu transcription.

name: Abdülkadir
desc: Turkish form of Abd al-Qadir.

name: Abdülkerim
desc: Turkish form of Abd al-Karim.

name: Abdulla
usage: Uzbek, Kyrgyz, Kazakh, Azerbaijani, Dhivehi, Uyghur, Arabic
desc: Form of Abd Allah in several languages, as well as an alternate transcription of the Arabic name.

name: Abdullaahi
desc: Fula form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdullah
usage: Arabic, Turkish, Urdu, Bengali, Malay, Indonesian
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الله (see Abd Allah), as well as the regular form in several other languages.

name: Abdullahi
desc: Hausa form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdüllatif
desc: Turkish form of Abd al-Latif.

name: Abdullo
desc: Tajik and Uzbek form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdullohi
desc: Tajik variant form of Abd Allah.

name: Abdul Rahman
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحمٰن (see Abd ar-Rahman), as well as the regular Malay form.

name: Abdurakhman
desc: Chechen form of Abd ar-Rahman.

name: Abdur Rahim
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحيم (see Abd ar-Rahim).

name: Abdur Rahman
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرحمٰن (see Abd ar-Rahman), as well as the usual Bengali transcription.

name: Abdur Rashid
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد الرشيد (see Abd ar-Rashid), as well as the usual Bengali transcription.

name: Abdus Salam
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عبد السلام (see Abd as-Salam), as well as the usual Bengali transcription.

name: Abduweli
desc: Uyghur form of Abd al-Wali.

name: Abe 1
desc: Short form of Abraham.

name: Abe 2
desc: Originally a Frisian short form of Adalbert (and other names starting with the Old German element adal "noble" and a second element beginning with b).

name: Abeba
desc: Means "flower" in Amharic.

name: Abednego
desc: Means "servant of Nebo" in Akkadian, Nebo being the Babylonian god of wisdom. In the Old Testament Abednego is the Babylonian name given to Azariah, one of the three men cast into a blazing furnace but saved from harm by God, as told in the Book of Daniel.

name: Abegail
desc: Variant of Abigail.

name: Ábel
desc: Hungarian form of Abel.

name: Abel
usage: English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Georgian, Armenian, Biblical, Biblical Latin, Biblical Greek
desc: From the Hebrew name הֶבֶל (Hevel) meaning "breath". In the Old Testament he is the second son of Adam and Eve, murdered out of envy by his brother Cain. In England, this name came into use during the Middle Ages, and it was common during the Puritan era.

name: Abele
desc: Italian form of Abel.

name: Abelone
desc: Danish form of Apollonia.

name: Abena
desc: Means "born on Tuesday" in Akan.

name: Abene
desc: Derived from Basque abe meaning "pillar". It is a Basque equivalent of Pilar.

name: Abeni
desc: Means "we prayed and we received" in Yoruba.

name: Abenner
desc: Biblical Greek form of Abner.

name: Aberash
desc: Means "giving off light, shining" in Amharic.

name: Abessa
desc: Biblical Greek form of Abishai.

name: Abessalom
desc: Biblical Greek form of Absalom.

name: Abha
desc: Means "splendour, light" in Sanskrit.

name: Abhay
desc: Means "fearless" in Sanskrit.

name: Abhijeet
desc: Alternate transcription of Hindi/Marathi अभिजीत or अभिजित or Bengali অভিজিৎ (see Abhijit).

name: Abhijit
desc: From Sanskrit अभिजित (abhijita) meaning "victorious". This is the Sanskrit name for the star Vega.

name: Abhilash
desc: Means "desire, wish" in Sanskrit.

name: Abhilasha
desc: Feminine form of Abhilash.

name: Abhinav
desc: Means "young, fresh" in Sanskrit.

name: Abhishek
usage: Indian, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil
desc: Means "anointing" in Sanskrit.

name: Abi
desc: Diminutive of Abigail (typically British).

name: Abia
desc: Biblical Greek and Latin form of Abijah.

name: Abiah
desc: Variant of Abijah, which also appears in the English Bible.

name: Abiathar
desc: From Hebrew אֶבְיָתָר ('Evyatar) meaning "my father abounds" or "my father excels". In the Old Testament Abiathar was a high priest during the reign of King David.

name: Abidan
desc: Means "my father is judge" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament he is a Benjamite prince.

name: Abidemi
desc: Means "born in my absence" in Yoruba. It is typically given to children born when the father is away.

name: Abiel
desc: Means "God is my father" in Hebrew. This was the name of the grandfather of Saul in the Old Testament.

name: Abigaëlle
desc: Variant of Abigaïl.

name: Abigaia
desc: Greek form of Abigail.

name: Abigaíl
desc: Spanish form of Abigail.

name: Abigaïl
desc: French form of Abigail.

name: Abigail
usage: English, Biblical, Biblical German, Biblical Italian, Biblical Portuguese, Biblical Latin
desc: From the Hebrew name אֲבִיגָיִל ('Avigayil) meaning "my father is joy", derived from the roots אָב ('av) meaning "father" and גִּיל (gil) meaning "joy". In the Old Testament this is the name of Nabal's wife. After Nabal's death she became the third wife of King David.... [more]

name: Abigale
desc: Variant of Abigail.

name: Abigayle
desc: Variant of Abigail.

name: Abigél
desc: Hungarian form of Abigail.

name: Abihu
desc: Means "he is my father" in Hebrew. This is the name of a son of Aaron in the Old Testament. He and his brother Nadab were killed by God because they presented him with unauthorized fire.

name: Abijah
desc: Means "my father is Yahweh" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of several characters, both male and female, including the second king of Judah (also known as Abijam).

name: Abilene
desc: From a place name mentioned briefly in the New Testament. It is probably from Hebrew אָבֵל ('avel) meaning "meadow, grassy area". It has occasionally been used as a given name in modern times.

name: Abílio
desc: Portuguese form of Avilius.

name: Abilio
desc: Spanish form of Avilius.

name: Abimael
desc: Meaning uncertain, though the first element is likely Hebrew אָב ('av) meaning "father". In the Old Testament he is listed as a descendant of Shem.

name: Abimbola
desc: Means "born to me with wealth" in Yoruba.

name: Abimelech
desc: Means "my father is king" in Hebrew, derived from the roots אָב ('av) meaning "father" and מֶלֶכְ (melekh) meaning "king". This is the name of several characters in the Old Testament including a king of Gerar who takes Abraham's wife Sarah, but is forced by God to give her back.

name: Abiodun
desc: Means "born on a festival" in Yoruba.

name: Abiola
desc: Means "born into wealth" in Yoruba.

name: Abioye
desc: Means "born into royalty" in Yoruba.

name: Abiram
desc: Means "my father is exalted" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament, Abiram is swallowed by an earthquake after rebelling against the leadership of Moses.

name: Abisai
desc: Biblical Latin form of Abishai.

name: Abishag
desc: Means "my father strays" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament Abishag is a young woman who tends King David in his old age.

name: Abishai
desc: Means "my father is a gift" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament he is one of King David's heroes.

name: Abital
desc: Means "my father is dew" in Hebrew. She is the fifth wife of David in the Old Testament.

name: 'Abla
desc: Means "full-figured" in Arabic. The 7th-century Arabic poet Antara dedicated much of his poetry to a woman named Abla.

name: Abner
desc: Means "my father is a light" in Hebrew, from אָב ('av) meaning "father" and נֵר (ner) meaning "lamp, light". In the Old Testament, Abner was a cousin of Saul and the commander of his army. After he killed Asahel he was himself slain by Asahel's brother Joab.... [more]

name: Abolfazl
desc: Persian form of Abu al-Fadl.

name: Abosede
desc: Means "comes with the start of the week" in Yoruba, given when the child is born on Sunday.

name: Aboubacar
desc: Form of Abu Bakr used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Abraam
desc: Biblical Greek form of Abraham, as well as a Georgian form.

name: Abraão
desc: Portuguese form of Abraham.

name: Ábrahám
desc: Hungarian form of Abraham.

name: Abraham
usage: English, Hebrew, Spanish, French, Swedish, Dutch, German (Rare), Norwegian (Rare), Danish (Rare), Biblical, Biblical Latin
desc: This name may be viewed either as meaning "father of many" in Hebrew or else as a contraction of Abram 1 and הָמוֹן (hamon) meaning "many, multitude". The biblical patriarch Abraham was originally named Abram but God changed his name (see Genesis 17:5). With his father Terah, he led his wife Sarah, his nephew Lot and their other followers from Ur into Canaan. He is regarded by Jews as being the founder of the Hebrews through his son Isaac and by Muslims as being the founder of the Arabs through his son Ishmael.... [more]

name: Abrahán
desc: Spanish form of Abraham.

name: Abram 1
desc: Means "high father" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament God changed Abram's name to Abraham (see Genesis 17:5).

name: Abram 2
desc: Russian and Georgian form of Abraham.

name: Abramo
desc: Italian form of Abraham.

name: Abrar
desc: Means "virtuous" in Arabic. It is typically feminine in the Arab world, and typically masculine in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh.

name: Abrasha
desc: Russian diminutive of Abraham.

name: Abril
desc: Spanish and Catalan form of April.

name: Absalom
desc: From the Hebrew name אַבְשָׁלוֹם ('Avshalom) meaning "my father is peace", derived from אָב ('av) meaning "father" and שָׁלוֹם (shalom) meaning "peace". In the Old Testament he is a son of King David. He avenged his sister Tamar by arranging the murder of her rapist, their half-brother Amnon. He later led a revolt against his father. While fleeing on the back of a mule he got his head caught in a tree and was killed by Joab.

name: Abu
desc: Means "father of" in Arabic. This is commonly used as an element in a kunya, which is a type of Arabic nickname. The element is combined with the name of one of the bearer's children (usually the eldest son). In some cases the kunya is figurative, not referring to an actual child, as in the case of the Muslim caliph Abu Bakr.

name: Abu al-Fadl
desc: Combination of Abu and Fadl. This was another name for Abbas, the son of the fourth caliph Ali.

name: Abubakar
desc: Form of Abu Bakr used in Nigeria.

name: Abu Bakr
desc: Combination of Abu and Bakr. Abu Bakr was a companion and father-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the first caliph of the Muslim world. His name was in fact a kunya (a nickname) formed using Abu; his real name was Abd Allah. Shia Muslims hold a more negative view of Abu Bakr, hence this name is more widely used among Sunnis.

name: Abul-Fazl
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic أبو الفضل (see Abu al-Fadl).

name: Abundio
desc: Spanish form of Abundius.

name: Abundius
desc: From Latin abundus meaning "abundant, plentiful". This was the name of several early saints, including a 5th-century bishop of Como.

name: Aca
desc: Serbian and Macedonian diminutive of Aleksandar.

name: Acacia
desc: From the name of a type of tree, ultimately derived from Greek ἀκή (ake) meaning "thorn, point".

name: Acacius
desc: Latinized form of Akakios.

name: Acantha
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἄκανθα (Akantha), which meant "thorn, prickle". In Greek legend she was a nymph loved by Apollo.

name: Ace 1
desc: From the English word meaning "highest rank". More commonly a nickname, it is occasionally used as a given name.

name: Ace 2
desc: Macedonian diminutive of Aleksandar.

name: Achaab
desc: Biblical Greek form of Ahab.

name: Achab
desc: Latin form of Ahab used in some versions of the Vulgate.

name: Achaemenes
desc: Latin form of Ἀχαιμένης (Achaimenes), the Greek form of the Old Persian name 𐏃𐎧𐎠𐎶𐎴𐎡𐏁 (Haxamaniš), derived from Old Iranian *haxa "friend, companion, ally" and *manah "mind, intellect, thought". This was the name of the founder of the Achaemenid dynasty (7th century BC).

name: Achaicus
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀχαϊκός (Achaikos), which referred to the region in Greece called Ἀχαΐα (Achaia), situated on the northern coast of the Peloponnese. In the New Testament this is the name of a Corinthian Christian who aids Saint Paul.

name: Achaikos
desc: Greek form of Achaicus.

name: Achaimenes
desc: Greek form of Achaemenes.

name: Achan
desc: Possibly a variation of the Hebrew word עֲכָר ('akhar) meaning "trouble". In the Old Testament, Achan is stoned to death because he steals forbidden items during the assault on Jericho.

name: Achard
desc: Medieval Norman form of Ekkehard.

name: 'Achashwerosh
desc: Biblical Hebrew form of Ahasuerus.

name: 'Ach'av
desc: Biblical Hebrew form of Ahab.

name: Acheloios
desc: Ancient Greek form of Achelous.

name: Achelous
desc: From Greek Ἀχελώιος (Acheloios), which is of unknown meaning, possibly of Semitic origin. This was the name of a Greek god of water and rivers, in particular the Achelous River in western Greece. He fought with (and was defeated by) Herakles for the hand of Deianeira.

name: Achieng
desc: Feminine form of Ochieng.

name: Achille
desc: French and Italian form of Achilles.

name: Achilleas
desc: Modern Greek form of Achilles.

name: Achilles
desc: From the Greek Ἀχιλλεύς (Achilleus), which is of unknown meaning, perhaps derived from Greek ἄχος (achos) meaning "pain" or else from the name of the Achelous River. This was the name of a warrior in Greek legend, one of the central characters in Homer's Iliad. The bravest of the Greek heroes in the war against the Trojans, he was eventually killed by an arrow to his heel, the only vulnerable part of his body.... [more]

name: Achilleus
desc: Ancient Greek form of Achilles.

name: Achim 1
desc: German short form of Joachim.

name: Achim 2
desc: Possibly means "he will establish" in Hebrew. In the New Testament this name is listed as an ancestor of Jesus.

name: Achinoam
desc: Hebrew form of Ahinoam.

name: Achsah
desc: Means "anklet, bangle" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of the daughter of Caleb.

name: Acke
desc: Swedish short form of Axel.

name: Aco
desc: Macedonian and Serbian diminutive of Aleksandar.

name: Ad
desc: Short form of Adriaan.

name: Ada 1
usage: English, Italian, Spanish, German, Dutch, Norwegian, Polish, Hungarian, Finnish, Germanic
desc: Originally a short form of Germanic names such as Adelaide or Adelina that begin with the element adal meaning "noble". Saint Ada was a 7th-century Frankish abbess at Le Mans. This name was also borne by Augusta Ada King (1815-1852), the Countess of Lovelace (known as Ada Lovelace), a daughter of Lord Byron. She was an assistant to Charles Babbage, the inventor of an early mechanical computer.

name: Ada 2
desc: Means "island" in Turkish.

name: Adad
desc: Akkadian cognate of Hadad.

name: Adad-Nirari
desc: Means "Adad is my helper", from the god's name Adad combined with Akkadian nērāru meaning "helper". This name was borne by three kings of the Assyrian Empire.

name: Adaeze
desc: Means "eldest daughter of the king" in Igbo.

name: Adah
desc: Means "adornment, ornament" in Hebrew. This was the name of the wives of both Lamech and Esau in the Old Testament.

name: Adaiah
desc: From the Hebrew name עֲדָיָה ('Adayah) meaning "Yahweh has adorned". This is the name of numerous Old Testament characters, including the father of Jedidah.

name: Adair
desc: From an English surname that was derived from the given name Edgar.

name: Adalberht
desc: Old German form of Albert.

name: Adalbern
desc: Derived from the Old German elements adal "noble" and bern "bear".

name: Adalbert
desc: Old German form of Albert. This is the name of a patron saint of Bohemia, Poland and Prussia. He is known by his birth name Vojtěch in Czech and Wojciech in Polish.

name: Adalberto
desc: Variant of Alberto.

name: Adalet
desc: Means "justice" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic عَدَلَ ('adala) meaning "to act justly".

name: Adalfarus
desc: Derived from the Old German elements adal "noble" and fara "journey".

name: Adalfuns
desc: Old German form of Alfonso.

name: Adalgard
desc: Old German form of Edelgard.

name: Adalgund
desc: Derived from the Old German elements adal "noble" and gunda "battle". See also Aldegund.

name: Adalhaid
desc: Old German form of Adelaide.

name: Adalhard
desc: Derived from the Old German elements adal "noble" and hart "hard, firm, brave, hardy". Saint Adalhard or Adalard was a cousin of Charlemagne who became an abbot of Corbie.

name: Adalheidis
desc: Old German form of Adelaide.

name: Adalia
desc: Meaning unknown, possibly of Persian origin. In Book of Esther in the Old Testament this is the name of a son of Haman the Agagite.

name: Adalindis
desc: Variant of Adallinda.

name: Adaline
desc: Variant of Adelina.

name: Adallinda
desc: Derived from the Old German elements adal "noble" and lind "soft, flexible, tender". Adallinda (or Adalindis or Ethelind) was the name of one of the concubines of Charlemagne, with whom she had at least two children.

name: Adalwin
desc: From the Old German elements adal "noble" and wini "friend" (a cognate of Æðelwine).

name: Adalwolf
desc: Old German form of Adolf.

name: 'Adalya'
desc: Hebrew form of Adalia.

name: Adalyn
desc: Variant of Adeline using the popular name suffix lyn.

name: Adalynn
desc: Variant of Adeline using the popular name suffix lynn.

name: Ádám
desc: Hungarian form of Adam.

name: Adam
usage: English, French, German, Polish, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Czech, Slovak, Russian, Ukrainian, Croatian, Serbian, Macedonian, Romanian, Catalan, Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Georgian, Biblical, Biblical Latin, Biblical Greek, Biblical Hebrew
desc: This is the Hebrew word for "man". It could be ultimately derived from Hebrew אדם ('adam) meaning "to be red", referring to the ruddy colour of human skin, or from Akkadian adamu meaning "to make".... [more]

name: Adamantios
desc: Derived from Greek ἀδάμας (adamas) meaning "unconquerable, unbreakable, adamant" (genitive ἀδάμαντος).

name: Adamina
desc: Feminine form of Adam.

name: Adamo
desc: Italian form of Adam.

name: Adamou
desc: Form of Adam used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Adamu
desc: Old Church Slavic form of Adam.

name: Adán
desc: Spanish form of Adam.

name: Adanna
desc: Means "eldest daughter of the father" in Igbo.

name: Adannaya
desc: Means "eldest daughter of her father" in Igbo.

name: Adão
desc: Portuguese form of Adam.

name: Adara
desc: Means "noble" in Hebrew.

name: Adas
desc: Short form of names beginning with Ad, such as Adomas or Adolfas.

name: Adawosgi
desc: Means "he is swimming" in Cherokee, from ᎠᏓᏬᏍᎬ (adawosgun) meaning "swimming".

name: 'Adayah
desc: Biblical Hebrew form of Adaiah.

name: Adde
desc: Variant of Ade 2.

name: Addie
desc: Diminutive of Adelaide, Adeline, Addison and other names containing the same sound.

name: Addilyn
desc: Variant of Adeline using the popular name suffix lyn.

name: Addison
desc: From an English surname meaning "son of Adam". Its recent popularity as a feminine name stems from its similarity in sound to Madison.

name: Addolorata
desc: Means "grieving" in Italian, from the title of the Virgin Mary, Maria Addolorata. It is most common in southern Italy. It is the equivalent of Spanish Dolores.

name: Addy 1
desc: Diminutive of Adelaide, Adeline, Addison and other names containing the same sound.

name: Addy 2
desc: Medieval diminutive of Adam.

name: Addyson
desc: Feminine variant of Addison.

name: Ade 1
desc: From Yoruba adé meaning "crown", also a short form of other names beginning with this element.

name: Ade 2
desc: Originally a short form of Germanic names beginning with the element adal meaning "noble".

name: Adebayo
desc: Means "the crown meets joy" in Yoruba.

name: Adebola
desc: Means "the crown meets wealth" in Yoruba.

name: Adebowale
desc: Means "the crown has returned home" in Yoruba.

name: Adedayo
desc: Means "the crown becomes joy" in Yoruba.

name: Adegoke
desc: Means "the crown has ascended the mountain" in Yoruba.

name: Adekunle
desc: Means "the crown has filled the home" in Yoruba.

name: Adél
desc: Hungarian form of Adela.

name: Adel
desc: Persian form of Adil, as well as an alternate transcription of the Arabic name.

name: Adéla
desc: Czech form of Adela.

name: Adela
usage: English, Spanish, Romanian, Polish, Slovak, Germanic
desc: Originally a short form of names beginning with the Old German element adal meaning "noble" (Proto-Germanic *aþalaz). Saint Adela was a 7th-century Frankish princess who founded a monastery at Pfazel in France. This name was also borne by a daughter of William the Conqueror.

name: Adelaida
desc: Spanish form of Adelaide.

name: Adélaïde
desc: French form of Adelaide.

name: Adelaide
desc: Means "nobleness, nobility", from the French form of the Germanic name Adalheidis, which was composed of adal "noble" and the suffix heit "kind, sort, type". It was borne in the 10th century by Saint Adelaide, the wife of the Holy Roman emperor Otto the Great.... [more]

name: Adelais
desc: Shortened form of Adalheidis.

name: Adelajda
desc: Polish form of Adelaide.

name: Adélard
desc: French form of Adalhard.

name: Adelardo
desc: Spanish and Italian form of Adalhard.

name: Adelbert
desc: German and Dutch variant of Adalbert.

name: Adèle
desc: French form of Adela.

name: Adele
desc: Form of Adela used in several languages. A famous bearer was the dancer and actress Adele Astaire (1896-1981). It was also borne by the British singer Adele Adkins (1988-), known simply as Adele. Shortly after she released her debut album in 2008 the name reentered the American top 1000 chart after 40-year absence.

name: Adelė
desc: Lithuanian form of Adela.

name: Adelgundis
desc: Latinized form of Adalgund.

name: Adelheid
desc: German and Dutch form of Adelaide.

name: Adelia
desc: Elaborated form of Adela.

name: Adélie
desc: Elaborated form of Adèle. Adélie Land in Antarctica was named in 1840 by the French explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville in honour of his wife Adèle (who was sometimes called Adélie).

name: Adelina
usage: Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Romanian, Bulgarian, Germanic (Latinized)
desc: From a Germanic name that was derived from the element adal meaning "noble" (Proto-Germanic *aþalaz).

name: Adelinde
desc: German form of Adallinda.

name: Adeline
desc: French and English form of Adelina.

name: Adelita
desc: Spanish diminutive of Adela. It is used especially in Mexico, where it is the name of a folk song about a female soldier.

name: Adella
desc: Variant of Adela.

name: Adelle
desc: Variant of Adele.

name: Adelma
desc: Feminine form of Adelmo. This name was used by Carlo Gozzi for a character in his play Turandot (1762).

name: Adelmar
desc: From the Old German elements adal "noble" and mari "famous". It is a cognate of the Old English name Æðelmær.

name: Adelmo
desc: Italian form of Adhelm, also used to refer to the English saint Ealdhelm.

name: Adelyn
desc: Variant of Adeline using the popular name suffix lyn.

name: Adelynn
desc: Variant of Adeline using the popular name suffix lynn.

name: Adem
desc: Turkish, Bosnian and Albanian form of Adam.

name: Ademar
desc: Portuguese form of Audamar (see Otmar).

name: Ademaro
desc: Italian form of Audamar (see Otmar).

name: Ademir
desc: Brazilian variant of Ademar.

name: Ademola
desc: Means "the crown is with wealth" in Yoruba.

name: Aden
desc: Variant of Aidan.

name: Adena
desc: Possibly a variant of Adina 1.

name: Adenike
desc: Means "the crown is to be cared for" in Yoruba.

name: Adeodatus
desc: Latin name meaning "given by God". This was the name of a son of Saint Augustine and two popes (who are also known by the related name Deusdedit).

name: Adeola
desc: Means "the crown of wealth" in Yoruba. It is also a surname.

name: Aderyn
desc: Means "bird" in Welsh. This is a modern Welsh name.

name: Adetokunbo
desc: Means "the crown returns from over the sea" in Yoruba.

name: Adewale
desc: Means "the crown has come home" in Yoruba.

name: Ádhamh
desc: Irish form of Adam.

name: Adhara
desc: Derived from Arabic عذارى ('adhara) meaning "maidens". This is the name of the second brightest star (after Sirius) in the constellation Canis Major.

name: Adhelm
desc: From the Old German elements atto meaning "father" and helm meaning "helmet, protection".

name: Adhiambo
desc: Feminine form of Odhiambo.

name: Adi 1
desc: Means "jewel, ornament" in Hebrew.

name: Adi 2
desc: Means "first" in Indonesian, ultimately from Sanskrit आदि (adi).

name: Adi 3
desc: Diminutive of Adolf (German) or Adrian (Romanian) as well as other names beginning with the same sound.

name: Adil
desc: Means "fair, honest, just" in Arabic, from the root عَدَلَ ('adala) meaning "to act justly". This name was borne by several sultans of Bijapur.

name: Adila
desc: Feminine form of Adil.

name: Adilə
desc: Azerbaijani feminine form of Adil.

name: Adile
desc: Turkish and Albanian feminine form of Adil.

name: Adilet
desc: Means "justice" in Kyrgyz and Kazakh, ultimately from Arabic عَدَلَ ('adala) meaning "to act justly".

name: Adin
desc: Meaning unknown, possibly from Turkish ad meaning "name".

name: Adina 1
usage: Biblical, Biblical Latin, Biblical Greek, Hebrew
desc: From Hebrew עֲדִינָא ('adina') meaning "delicate". This name is borne by a soldier in the Old Testament. It is also used in modern Hebrew as a feminine name, typically spelled עֲדִינָה.

name: Adina 2
desc: Meaning uncertain, possibly a short form of Adelina.

name: 'Adinah
desc: Hebrew form of Adina 1.

name: Adino
desc: Means "ornament" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of one of King David's mighty men.

name: Adir
desc: Means "strong, mighty" in Hebrew. This word is used in the Hebrew Bible to describe God.

name: Adisa
desc: Means "bundled up and set to dry" in Yoruba.

name: Aditi
usage: Hinduism, Indian, Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Kannada
desc: Means "boundless, entire" or "freedom, security" in Sanskrit. This is the name of an ancient Hindu goddess of the sky and fertility. According to the Vedas she is the mother of the gods.

name: Aditya
usage: Hinduism, Indian, Hindi, Marathi, Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Nepali, Indonesian
desc: Means "belonging to Aditi" in Sanskrit. This is a name for the seven (or eight) Hindu gods who are the children of Aditi. It is also another name for the sun god Surya.

name: Adjoa
desc: Variant of Adwoa.

name: Adlai
desc: Contracted form of Adalia. This is the name of the father of one of King David's herdsmen in the Old Testament.

name: Adler
desc: From a German surname meaning "eagle".

name: Admetos
desc: Greek form of Admetus.

name: Admetus
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἄδμητος (Admetos) meaning "unconquered, untamed", a poetic form of ἀδάμαστος (adamastos). In Greek mythology this was the name of a king of Pherae in Thessaly. He was the husband of Alcestis, who died for him.

name: Admir
desc: Meaning uncertain. It might be a variant of Amir 1 or it could be derived from Latin admiror meaning "admire".

name: Adna
desc: Feminine form of Adnan.

name: Adnan
desc: Means "settler" in Arabic. According to tradition, Adnan was an ancestor of the Prophet Muhammad and the northern Arabian tribes.

name: Adolf
usage: German, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Germanic
desc: From the Old German name Adalwolf, which meant "noble wolf" from the elements adal "noble" and wolf. It was borne by several Swedish kings as a first or second name, most notably by Gustav II Adolf in the 17th century. Association with Adolf Hitler (1889-1945), the leader of the Nazi party in Germany during World War II, has lessened the use of this name.

name: Adolfas
desc: Lithuanian form of Adolf.

name: Adolfito
desc: Spanish diminutive of Adolfo.

name: Adolfo
desc: Italian and Spanish form of Adolf.

name: Adolph
desc: English form of Adolf, rarely used since World War II.

name: Adolphe
desc: French form of Adolf, rarely used since World War II.

name: Adolphus
desc: Latinized form of Adolf.

name: Adomas
desc: Lithuanian form of Adam.

name: Adonai
desc: Means "my lord" in Hebrew. This was the title used to refer to the God of the Israelites, Yahweh, whose name was forbidden to be spoken.

name: Adonay
desc: Spanish variant of Adonai.

name: Adone
desc: Italian form of Adonis.

name: Adonijah
desc: Means "my lord is Yahweh" in Hebrew. This is the name of one of King David's sons in the Old Testament. Though he was the eldest surviving son of David, he was passed over as heir to the throne in favour of Solomon.

name: Adoniram
desc: Means "my lord is exalted" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of an overseer of tribute under the kings David, Solomon and Rehoboam. He was stoned to death when the Israelites revolted.

name: Adonis
desc: From Phoenician 𐤀𐤃𐤍 (ʾadon) meaning "lord, master". In Greek myth Adonis was a handsome young shepherd killed while hunting a wild boar. The anemone flower is said to have sprung from his blood. Because he was loved by Aphrodite, Zeus allowed him to be restored to life for part of each year. The Greeks borrowed this character from Semitic traditions, originally Sumerian (see Dumuzi).

name: 'Adoniyah
desc: Hebrew form of Adonijah.

name: Adora
desc: Short form of Adoración.

name: Adoración
desc: Means "adoration" in Spanish. This name refers to the event that is known in Christian tradition as the Adoration of the Magi, which is when the three Magi presented gifts to the infant Jesus and worshipped him.

name: Adorinda
desc: Means "adorable" in Esperanto.

name: Adorján
desc: Hungarian form of Adrian.

name: Adrastea
desc: Latinized form of Adrasteia. One of Jupiter's moons bears this name.

name: Adrasteia
desc: Feminine form of Adrastos. In Greek mythology this name was borne by a nymph who fostered the infant Zeus. This was also another name of the goddess Nemesis.

name: Adrastos
desc: Means "not inclined to run away" in Greek, from the negative prefix ἀ (a) and διδράσκω (didrasko) meaning "to run away". This was the name of a king of Argos in Greek legend.

name: Adria
desc: Short form of Adriana.

name: Adrià
desc: Catalan form of Adrian.

name: Adriaan
desc: Dutch form of Adrian.

name: Adrián
desc: Spanish, Hungarian and Slovak form of Hadrianus (see Hadrian).

name: Adrian
usage: English, Romanian, Polish, German, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Russian
desc: Form of Hadrianus (see Hadrian) used in several languages. Several saints and six popes have borne this name, including the only English pope, Adrian IV, and the only Dutch pope, Adrian VI. As an English name, it has been in use since the Middle Ages, though it was not popular until modern times.

name: Adriana
usage: Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Romanian, Polish, Slovak, Czech, Bulgarian, English, Dutch
desc: Feminine form of Adrian. A famous bearer is the Brazilian model Adriana Lima (1981-).

name: Adrianna
desc: Feminine form of Adrian.

name: Adrianne
desc: Feminine form of Adrian.

name: Adriano
desc: Italian and Portuguese form of Adrian.

name: Adrians
desc: Latvian form of Adrian.

name: Adrianus
desc: Official Dutch form of Adrian, used on birth certificates but not commonly in daily life.

name: Adriel
desc: Means "flock of God" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of a man who married Saul's daughter Merab.

name: Adrien
desc: French form of Adrian.

name: Adriene
desc: Brazilian variant of Adriana.

name: Adrienn
desc: Hungarian feminine form of Adrian.

name: Adrienne
desc: French feminine form of Adrian.

name: Adrijan
desc: Croatian and Macedonian form of Adrian.

name: Adrijana
desc: Slovene, Serbian, Croatian and Macedonian feminine form of Adrian.

name: Adsila
desc: From Cherokee ᎠᏥᎳ (atsila) "fire" or ᎠᏥᎸᏍᎩ (atsilunsgi) "flower, blossom".

name: Adva
desc: Means "small wave, ripple" in Hebrew.

name: Adwoa
desc: Means "born on Monday" in Akan.

name: Adzo
desc: Ewe form of Adwoa.

name: Æbbe
desc: Old English form of Ebba 2.

name: Áed
desc: Old Irish form of Aodh.

name: Áedán
desc: Old Irish form of Aodhán.

name: Áedh
desc: Variant of Áed.

name: Áednat
desc: Feminine form of Áed.

name: Aegidius
desc: Original Latin form of Giles.

name: Ægir
desc: Means "sea, ocean" in Old Norse. According to Norse mythology Ægir was a god or giant (jǫtunn) who lived under the ocean. His wife was Rán.

name: Aegle
desc: Latinized form of the Greek Αἴγλη (Aigle), which meant "light, radiance, glory". This was the name of several characters in Greek myth, including one of the Heliades and one of the Hesperides.

name: Ælfflæd
desc: Old English name composed of the elements ælf "elf" and flæd, possibly meaning "beauty".

name: Ælfgar
desc: Old English form of Algar.

name: Ælfgifu
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and giefu "gift". This was the name of the first wife of the English king Æðelræd II.

name: Ælfheah
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and heah "high". This was the name of an 11th-century archbishop of Canterbury, a saint and martyr, who is commonly known as Alphege or Elphege.

name: Ælfnoð
desc: Derived from the Old English element ælf "elf" combined with noð "boldness, daring".

name: Ælfræd
desc: Old English form of Alfred.

name: Ælfric
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and ric "ruler, king" (making it a cognate of Alberich). This was the name of a 10th-century archbishop of Canterbury, sometimes considered a saint.

name: Ælfsige
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and sige "victory".

name: Ælfstan
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and stan "stone".

name: Ælfswiþ
desc: Derived from the Old English element ælf "elf" combined with swiþ "strong".

name: Ælfþryð
desc: Old English form of Elfreda.

name: Ælfthryth
desc: Variant of Ælfþryð (see Elfreda).

name: Ælfweard
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and weard "guardian".

name: Ælfwig
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and wig "war, battle".

name: Ælfwine
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and wine "friend". This name was not commonly used after the Norman Conquest.

name: Ælfwynn
desc: Derived from the Old English elements ælf "elf" and wynn "joy". This name was borne by a daughter of Æðelflæd who ruled Mercia briefly in the 10th century.

name: Aelia
desc: Feminine form of Aelius.

name: Aeliana
desc: Feminine form of Aelianus.

name: Aelianus
desc: Roman cognomen that was a derivative of Aelius.

name: Aelita
desc: Created by Russian author Aleksey Tolstoy for his science fiction novel Aelita (1923), where it belongs to a Martian princess. In the book, the name is said to mean "starlight seen for the last time" in the Martian language.

name: Aelius
desc: Roman family name that was possibly derived from the Greek word ἥλιος (helios) meaning "sun". This was the family name of the Roman emperor Hadrian.

name: Aella
desc: Means "whirlwind" in Greek. In Greek myth this was the name of an Amazon warrior killed by Herakles during his quest for Hippolyta's girdle.

name: Ælred
desc: Contracted form of Æðelræd. This was the name of a 12th-century English saint.

name: Aemilia
desc: Feminine form of Aemilius (see Emily).

name: Aemiliana
desc: Feminine form of Aemilianus (see Emiliano).

name: Aemilianus
desc: Original Latin form of Emiliano.

name: Aemilius
desc: Original Latin form of Emil.

name: Aeneas
desc: Latin form of the Greek name Αἰνείας (Aineias), derived from Greek αἴνη (aine) meaning "praise". In Greek legend he was a son of Aphrodite and was one of the chief heroes who defended Troy from the Greeks. The Roman poet Virgil continued his story in the Aeneid, in which Aeneas travels to Italy and founds the Roman state.

name: Aengus
desc: Older form of Aonghus.

name: Aenoheso
desc: Means "little hawk", from Cheyenne aénohe "hawk" and the diminutive suffix -so.

name: Aenor
desc: Probably a Latinized form of a Germanic name of unknown meaning. This was the name of the mother of Eleanor of Aquitaine.

name: Aeolus
desc: Latinized form of Aiolos.

name: Aeron
desc: From the name of the Welsh river Aeron, itself probably derived from the hypothetical Celtic goddess Agrona. Alternatively, the name could be taken from Welsh aeron meaning "berries".

name: Aerona
desc: Variant of Aeron.

name: Aeronwen
desc: Combination of Aeron and the Welsh element gwen meaning "white, blessed".

name: Aeronwy
desc: Extended form of Aeron.

name: Æsc
desc: Means "ash tree" in Old English. This was the nickname of a 5th-century king of Kent, whose birth name was Oeric.

name: Aeschylus
desc: From the Greek name Αἰσχύλος (Aischylos), derived from αἶσχος (aischos) meaning "shame". This was the name of a 5th-century BC Athenian playwright, known for his tragedies.

name: Aesculapius
desc: Latinized form of Asklepios.

name: Aeson
desc: From the Greek Αἰσών (Aison), which is of unknown meaning. Aeson was the father of Jason in Greek mythology.

name: Aesop
desc: From the Greek Αἴσωπος (Aisopos), which is of unknown meaning. This was the name of a Greek fabulist of the 6th century BC, famous for such tales as The Tortoise and the Hare. Though his existence is uncertain, he was later said to have been a slave on the island of Samos.

name: Æþelbeorht
desc: Old English cognate of Adalbert (see Albert). This was the name of a Saxon king of England and two kings of Kent, one of whom was a saint. It became unused after the Normans introduced their form of Adalbert after their invasion.

name: Æðelberht
desc: Variant of Æþelbeorht.

name: Æðelflæd
desc: Old English name composed of the elements æðele "noble" and flæd, possibly meaning "beauty". This was the name of a 10th-century ruler of Mercia (a daughter of Alfred the Great).

name: Æthelflæd
desc: Variant of Æðelflæd.

name: Æðelfrið
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and friþ "peace". The name was rarely used after the Norman Conquest.

name: Æðelmær
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and mære "famous". A famous bearer was the 11th-century English monk Æðelmær of Malmesbury who attempted to fly with a gliding apparatus (breaking his legs in the process).

name: Æthelnoð
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and noð "boldness, daring".

name: Æðelræd
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and ræd "counsel, advice". This was the name of two Saxon kings of England including Æðelræd II "the Unready" whose realm was overrun by the Danes in the early 11th century. The name was rarely used after the Norman Conquest.

name: Æþelræd
desc: Variant of Æðelræd.

name: Æthelred
desc: Variant of Æðelræd.

name: Æðelric
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and ric "ruler, king". This was the name of several early Anglo-Saxon kings.

name: Æthelric
desc: Variant of Æðelric.

name: Æðelstan
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and stan "stone". This was the name of a 10th-century English king, the first to rule all of England. The name was rarely used after the Norman Conquest, though it enjoyed a modest revival (as Athelstan) in the 19th century.

name: Æthelstan
desc: Variant of Æðelstan.

name: Æðelþryð
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and þryþ "strength".

name: Æthelthryth
desc: Variant of Æðelþryð.

name: Æthelweald
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and weald "powerful, mighty".

name: Æthelweard
desc: Derived from the Old English element æðele "noble" combined with weard "guardian".

name: Æðelwine
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and wine "friend". This was the name of a few Anglo-Saxon saints, including a 7th-century bishop of Lindsey. The name became rare after the Norman Conquest.

name: Æthelwine
desc: Variant of Æðelwine.

name: Æðelwulf
desc: Derived from the Old English elements æðele "noble" and wulf "wolf" (making it a cognate of Adolf). This name was borne by a 9th-century king of Wessex.

name: Aether
desc: Latinized form of Greek Αἰθήρ (Aither) meaning "ether, heaven", derived from αἴθω (aitho) meaning "to burn, to ignite". In Greek mythology this was the name of the god of the upper sky.

name: Aetius
desc: Roman cognomen that was probably derived from Greek ἀετός (aetos) meaning "eagle". A famous bearer was the 5th-century Roman general Flavius Aetius, who defeated Attila the Hun at the Battle of Chalons.

name: Afaf
desc: Means "chastity" in Arabic.

name: Afan
desc: Bosnian form of Affan.

name: Afanasiy
desc: Russian form of Athanasius.

name: Afanasy
desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Афанасий (see Afanasiy).

name: Afërdita
desc: Means "daybreak, morning" in Albanian, from afër "nearby, close" and ditë "day". It is also used as an Albanian form of Aphrodite.

name: Affan
desc: From Arabic عفّ ('aff) meaning "chaste, modest, pure". This was the name of the father of the caliph Uthman.

name: Affraic
desc: Old Irish form of Aifric.

name: Afi
desc: Ewe form of Afua.

name: Afia
desc: Variant of Afua.

name: Afif
desc: Means "chaste" in Arabic.

name: Afina
desc: Russian and Ukrainian form of Athena.

name: Afolabi
desc: Means "born into wealth" in Yoruba.

name: Afon
desc: Means "river" in Welsh. This is a Welsh name of recent origin.

name: Afonso
desc: Portuguese and Galician form of Alfonso. This was the name of the first king of Portugual, ruling in the 12th century.

name: Afonya
desc: Diminutive of Afanasiy.

name: Afra 1
desc: Originally used by the Romans as a nickname for a woman from Africa. This was the name of two early saints.

name: Afra 2
desc: Means "whitish red" in Arabic.

name: África
desc: Spanish form of Africa 1. It is usually taken from the title of the Virgin Mary, Nuestra Señora de África, the patron saint of the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in North Africa.

name: Àfrica
desc: Catalan form of Africa 1.

name: Africa 1
desc: From the name of the continent, which is of Latin origin, possibly from the Afri people who lived near Carthage in North Africa. This rare name is used most often by African-American parents.

name: Africa 2
desc: Anglicized form of Aifric.

name: Africanus
desc: Roman cognomen derived from the place name Africa, which in Roman times referred only to North Africa. This was the agnomen of the 3rd-century BC Roman general Scipio Africanus, who was honoured with it after his victory over Carthage in the Second Punic War. His descendants used it as a cognomen.

name: Afrim
desc: Means "approach" in Albanian.

name: Afrodita
desc: Spanish and Russian form of Aphrodite.

name: Afrodite
desc: Italian and Portuguese form of Aphrodite.

name: Afroditi
desc: Modern Greek form of Aphrodite.

name: Afsaneh
desc: Means "legend, myth, fable" in Persian.

name: Afsoon
desc: Alternate transcription of Persian افسون (see Afsoun).

name: Afsoun
desc: Means "charm, spell" in Persian.

name: Afsun
desc: Alternate transcription of Persian افسون (see Afsoun).

name: Afua
desc: Means "born on Friday" in Akan.

name: Afzal
desc: Means "better, superior" in Arabic.

name: Agafon
desc: Russian form of Agathon.

name: Agafya
desc: Russian form of Agatha.

name: Agam
desc: Means "lake" in Hebrew.

name: Agamemnon
desc: Possibly means "very steadfast" in Greek. In Greek mythology he was the brother of Menelaus. He led the Greek expedition to Troy to recover his brother's wife Helen. After the Trojan War Agamemnon was killed by his wife Clytemnestra.

name: Agape
desc: Derived from Greek ἀγάπη (agape) meaning "love". This name was borne by at least two early saints.

name: Agapetos
desc: Ancient Greek form of Agapito.

name: Agapetus
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Agapetos (see Agapito).

name: Agapi
desc: Modern Greek form of Agape.

name: Agapios
desc: Masculine form of Agape. This was the name of a saint from Caesarea who was martyred during the persecutions of the Roman emperor Diocletian in the early 4th century.

name: Agapito
desc: From the Late Latin name Agapitus or Agapetus, which was derived from the Greek name Ἀγαπητός (Agapetos) meaning "beloved". The name Agapetus was borne by two popes.

name: Agapitos
desc: Modern Greek form of Agapito.

name: Agar
usage: Biblical Latin, Biblical Greek, Biblical French, Biblical Italian
desc: Form of Hagar used in the Greek and Latin Old Testament.

name: Ágata
desc: Spanish and Portuguese form of Agatha.

name: Agáta
desc: Czech and Slovak form of Agatha.

name: Agata
usage: Italian, Polish, Slovene, Russian, Croatian, Serbian, Swedish
desc: Form of Agatha in various languages.

name: Agatha
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀγαθή (Agathe), derived from Greek ἀγαθός (agathos) meaning "good". Saint Agatha was a 3rd-century martyr from Sicily who was tortured and killed after spurning the advances of a Roman official. The saint was widely revered in the Middle Ages, and her name has been used throughout Christian Europe (in various spellings). The mystery writer Agatha Christie (1890-1976) was a famous modern bearer of this name.

name: Agathangelos
desc: Means "bearer of good news", derived from Greek ἀγαθός (agathos) meaning "good" and ἄγγελος (angelos) meaning "messenger, angel". Saint Agathangelus of Rome was a 4th-century deacon who was martyred during the persecutions of the emperor Diocletian.

name: Agathe
usage: French, German, Norwegian (Rare), Danish (Rare), Ancient Greek
desc: Form of Agatha in several languages.

name: Agathi
desc: Modern Greek form of Agatha.

name: Agathinos
desc: Greek form of Agathinus.

name: Agathinus
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἀγαθίνος (Agathinos), derived from ἀγαθός (agathos) meaning "good".

name: Agathon
desc: Greek masculine form of Agatha.

name: Agatino
desc: Italian form of Agathinus.

name: Agatka
desc: Polish diminutive of Agata.

name: Agaue
desc: Means "illustrious, noble" in Greek. This was the mother of Pentheus in Greek myth.

name: Agda
desc: Swedish variant form of Agatha.

name: Åge
desc: Norwegian form of Áki.

name: Age 1
desc: Frisian form of Ago.

name: Age 2
desc: Estonian form of Agnes.

name: Aggie
desc: Diminutive of Agnes or Agatha.

name: Aghavni
desc: Means "dove" in Armenian.

name: Aghi
desc: Old Norse form of Ove.

name: Aghil
desc: Persian form of Aqil.

name: Ági
desc: Diminutive of Ágota or Ágnes.

name: Agi
desc: Old German variant of Ago.

name: Agilulf
desc: Old German name derived from the elements agil meaning "edge, blade" and wolf meaning "wolf". This name was borne by a 6th-century king of the Lombards and by an 8th-century saint (a bishop of Cologne).

name: Agim
desc: Means "dawn" in Albanian.

name: Agimar
desc: Derived from the Old Frankish element aggju, Old High German ekka meaning "edge, blade" combined with mari meaning "famous".

name: Aglaé
desc: French form of Aglaia.

name: Aglaea
desc: Latinized form of Aglaia.

name: Aglaia
desc: Means "splendour, beauty" in Greek. In Greek mythology she was one of the three Graces or Χάριτες (Charites). This name was also borne by a 4th-century saint from Rome.

name: Aglaya
desc: Russian form of Aglaia.

name: Agmundr
desc: Old Norse form of Amund.

name: Agnar
desc: From the Old Norse name Agnarr, derived from agi "awe, fear" or egg "edge of a sword" combined with herr "army, warrior".

name: Agnarr
desc: Old Norse form of Agnar.

name: Agnė
desc: Lithuanian form of Agnes.

name: Agner
desc: Danish form of Agnar.

name: Ágnes
desc: Hungarian form of Agnes.

name: Agnès
desc: French and Catalan form of Agnes.

name: Agnes
usage: English, German, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Icelandic, Estonian, Ancient Greek (Latinized)
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἁγνή (Hagne), derived from Greek ἁγνός (hagnos) meaning "chaste". Saint Agnes was a virgin martyred during the persecutions of the Roman emperor Diocletian. The name became associated with Latin agnus "lamb", resulting in the saint's frequent depiction with a lamb by her side. Due to her renown, the name became common in Christian Europe.... [more]

name: Agneša
desc: Slovak variant of Agnes.

name: Agnesa
desc: Slovak and Albanian form of Agnes.

name: Agnese
desc: Italian and Latvian form of Agnes.

name: Agnessa
desc: Russian form of Agnes.

name: Agneta
desc: Swedish variant of Agnes.

name: Agnete
desc: Danish and Norwegian variant of Agnes.

name: Agnetha
desc: Swedish variant of Agnes.

name: Agnethe
desc: Danish and Norwegian variant of Agnes.

name: Agneza
desc: Croatian form of Agnes.

name: Agni 1
desc: Means "fire" in Sanskrit. This is the name of the ancient Hindu fire god, usually depicted as red-skinned with three legs, seven arms, and two faces.

name: Agni 2
desc: Modern Greek form of Agnes.

name: Agnia
desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Агния (see Agniya).

name: Agnieszka
desc: Polish form of Agnes.

name: Agnija
desc: Serbian, Macedonian and Latvian form of Agnes.

name: Agniya
desc: Russian form of Agnes.

name: Ago
desc: From the Old High German element ekka, Old Saxon eggia meaning "edge, blade" (Proto-Germanic *agjō). Alternatively it could be from Old High German egi meaning "fear" (Proto-Germanic *agaz). This was the name of a 7th-century Duke of Friuli.

name: Agostina
desc: Italian feminine form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Agostinho
desc: Portuguese form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Agostino
desc: Italian form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Ágoston
desc: Hungarian form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Ågot
desc: Norwegian variant form of Agatha.

name: Ágota
desc: Hungarian form of Agatha.

name: Agrafena
desc: Russian form of Agrippina.

name: Agripina
desc: Spanish form of Agrippina.

name: Agrippa
desc: Roman cognomen of unknown meaning, possibly from a combination of Greek ἄγριος (agrios) meaning "wild" and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse" or alternatively of Etruscan origin. It was also used as a praenomen, or given name, by the Furia and Menenia families. In the New Testament this name was borne by Herod Agrippa (a grandson of Herod the Great), the king of Israel who put the apostle James to death. It was also borne by the 1st-century BC Roman general Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa.

name: Agrippina
desc: Feminine derivative of Agrippa. This name was borne by the scheming mother of the Roman emperor Nero, who eventually had her killed. This was also the name of a 3rd-century Roman saint who is venerated in Sicily.

name: Agron
desc: Probably of Illyrian origin, maybe related to Albanian ag meaning "dawn". Alternatively it might be connected to Greek ἀγρός (agros) meaning "field". This was the name of a 3rd-century BC Illyrian king, the husband of Teuta.

name: Agrona
desc: Perhaps derived from the old Celtic root *agro- meaning "battle, slaughter". This is possibly the name of a Brythonic goddess for whom the River Ayr in Scotland and River Aeron in Wales were named.

name: Águeda
desc: Spanish and Portuguese form of Agatha.

name: Agung
desc: Means "great, large" in Indonesian.

name: Agurne
desc: From Basque agur meaning "greeting, salutation".

name: Agurtzane
desc: From Basque agurtza meaning "greeting, salutation".

name: Agus
desc: Variant of Bagus.

name: Agustí
desc: Catalan form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Agustín
desc: Spanish form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Agustina
desc: Spanish feminine form of Augustinus (see Augustine 1).

name: Ah
desc: From the Chinese character 阿 (ā), which has no distinct meaning. It is not normally given as a name, but it can be prefixed to another name to make it a diminutive.

name: Ahab
desc: Means "uncle", from Hebrew אָח ('ach) meaning "brother" and אָב ('av) meaning "father". This was the name of a king of Israel, the husband of Jezebel, as told in the Old Testament. He was admonished by Elijah for his sinful behaviour. Herman Melville later used this name in his novel Moby-Dick (1851), where it belongs to a sea captain obsessively hunting for a white whale.

name: Aharon
desc: Hebrew form of Aaron.

name: Ahasuerus
desc: From Hebrew אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ ('Achashwerosh), from the Old Persian name Xšayarša (see Xerxes). This name appears several times in the Old Testament belonging to a king of Persia. In the Book of Esther, Ahasuerus is the husband of Esther.

name: Ahava
desc: Means "love" in Hebrew.

name: Ahenobarbus
desc: From a Roman cognomen meaning "bronze beard" in Latin. This name was borne by a series of consuls of the late Roman Republic.

name: Ahinoam
desc: Means "my brother is pleasant" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is the name of wives of both Saul and David.

name: Əhməd
desc: Azerbaijani form of Ahmad.

name: Ahmad
usage: Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Bengali, Pashto, Indonesian, Malay, Avar
desc: Means "most commendable, most praiseworthy" in Arabic (a superlative form of Hamid 1).

name: Ahmadu
desc: Hausa form of Ahmad.

name: Ahmed
usage: Turkish, Bosnian, Dhivehi, Bengali, Arabic, Urdu, Pashto
desc: Variant of Ahmad. This was the name of three Ottoman sultans.

name: Ahmet
desc: Turkish form of Ahmad.

name: Ahmose
desc: From Egyptian jꜥḥ-ms meaning "born of Iah", derived from the name of the Egyptian god Iah combined with msj meaning "be born". This was the name of the first pharaoh of the 18th dynasty (16th century BC). He defeated the Hyksos and drove them from Egypt. It was also borne by others among Egyptian royalty from the same era, including several queens consort.

name: Aholibamah
desc: Means "tent of the high place" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament this is one of the wives of Esau, possibly the same as Judith.

name: Ahoth
desc: Form of Ehud used in the Latin Old Testament.

name: Ahriman
desc: Modern Persian form of Angra Mainyu.

name: Ahtahkakoop
desc: From Cree ᐊᑖᐦᑲᑯᐦᑊ (Atâhkakohp) meaning "star blanket", derived from ᐊᑖᕁ (atâhk) "star" and ᐊᑯᐦᑊ (akohp) "blanket". This was the name of an early 19th-century chief of a Plains Cree people.

name: Ahti
desc: Meaning unknown. This is the name of the Finnish god of the ocean, rivers and fishing.

name: Ahuludegi
desc: Means "he throws away the drum" from Cherokee ᎠᎱᎵ (ahuli) "drum" and ᎤᏕᎦ (udega) "throw". This was the name of a 19th-century Cherokee chief, also known as John Jolly.

name: Ahura Mazda
desc: Means "lord of wisdom", from Avestan 𐬀𐬵𐬎𐬭𐬀 (ahura) meaning "lord" and 𐬨𐬀𐬰𐬛𐬁 (mazdā) meaning "wisdom". In Zoroastrianism Ahura Mazda was the supreme creator, and the god of light, truth, and goodness.

name: Ahuva
desc: Means "beloved" in Hebrew.

name: Ai 1
desc: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection", 藍 (ai) meaning "indigo", or other kanji with the same pronunciation.

name: Ai 2
desc: From Chinese 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection", 蔼 (ǎi) meaning "friendly, lush", or other characters that are pronounced similarly.

name: Aias
desc: Greek form of Ajax.

name: Aibek
desc: Derived from Kazakh and Kyrgyz ай (ay) meaning "moon" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

name: Aíbinn
desc: Old Irish form of Aoibheann.

name: Aïcha
desc: Form of Aisha used in Northern Africa and other French-influenced regions of the continent.

name: Aïchatou
desc: Form of Aisha used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Aída
desc: Spanish form of Ayda.

name: Aida
desc: Variant of Ayda. This name was used in Verdi's opera Aida (1871), where it belongs to an Ethiopian princess held captive in Egypt.

name: Aidan
desc: Anglicized form of Aodhán. In the latter part of the 20th century it became popular in America due to its sound, since it shares a sound with such names as Braden and Hayden. It peaked ranked 39th for boys in 2003.

name: Aidana
desc: Means "wise moon" in Kazakh, from ай (ay) meaning "moon" and дана (dana) meaning "wise".

name: Aidas
desc: Means "echo" in Lithuanian.

name: Aiday
desc: Means "moon-like" in Kazakh, from ай (ay) meaning "moon" and the suffix дай (day) meaning "like".

name: Aideen
desc: Anglicized form of Éadaoin.

name: Aiden
desc: Variant of Aidan.

name: Aífe
desc: Old Irish form of Aoife.

name: Aifric
desc: From Old Irish Affraic, possibly from Afraicc, the Old Irish name of the continent of Africa (see Africa 1). Alternatively, it could be from *Aithbrecc, an unattested earlier form of Aithbhreac. This was the name of two abbesses of Kildare in the 8th and 9th centuries. It was also borne by a 12th-century daughter of the king of the Isle of Mann who married the Anglo-Norman knight John de Courcy.

name: Aiga
desc: Feminine form of Aigars.

name: Aigar
desc: Possibly from the Finnic root aika meaning "time" (Estonian aeg).

name: Aigars
desc: Probably from a Livonian name that was a cognate of Aigar.

name: Aigerim
desc: Means "wonderful moon", from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and керім (kerim) meaning "wonderful".

name: Aigle
desc: Greek form of Aegle.

name: Aignéis
desc: Irish form of Agnes.

name: Aigul
desc: Kazakh and Kyrgyz form of Aygül.

name: Aija
desc: Of uncertain meaning, possibly related to Latvian aijāt meaning "to rock, to lull". It was used by the Latvian writer Jānis Jaunsudrabiņš for the title character of his novel Aija (1911).

name: Aikaterine
desc: Ancient Greek form of Katherine.

name: Aikaterini
desc: Alternate transcription of Greek Αικατερίνη (see Ekaterini).

name: Aike
desc: Diminutive of names beginning with the Old German element ekka meaning "edge, blade" or adal meaning "noble".

name: Aiko
desc: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" and 子 (ko) meaning "child", as well as other character combinations.

name: Aikorkem
desc: Means "elegant moon", derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and көркем (korkem) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined, artistic".

name: Aila
desc: Finnish form of Áile.

name: Ailbe
desc: Old Irish form of Ailbhe.

name: Ailbhe
desc: From Old Irish Ailbe, possibly derived from the old Celtic root *albiyo- "world, light, white" or Old Irish ail "rock". In Irish legend this was the name of a female warrior of the Fianna. It was also the name of a 6th-century masculine saint, the founder of a monastery at Emly.

name: Áile
desc: Sami form of Helga.

name: Ailean
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Alan.

name: Aileas
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Alice.

name: Aileen
desc: Variant of Eileen.

name: Ailen
desc: Variant of Ayelen.

name: Aili
desc: Finnish and Estonian form of Áile.

name: Ailill
desc: Means "elf" in Irish. This name was borne by several early Irish kings. It also occurs frequently in Irish legend, borne for example by the husband of Queen Medb.

name: Ailín
desc: Possibly an Irish form of Alan or Ælfwine.

name: Ailin
desc: Kazakh form of Aylin.

name: Ailís
desc: Irish form of Alice.

name: Ailis
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Alice.

name: Ailish
desc: Anglicized form of Ailís.

name: Ailpean
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Alpin.

name: Ailsa
desc: From Ailsa Craig, the name of an island off the west coast of Scotland, which is of uncertain derivation.

name: Aiman 1
desc: Means "beauty of the moon" in Kazakh.

name: Aiman 2
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic أيمن (see Ayman).

name: Aimar
desc: Medieval Basque name, possibly derived from the Germanic name Agimar.

name: Aimé
desc: From Old French Amé, the masculine form of Amée (see Amy).

name: Aimée
desc: French form of Amy.

name: Aimee
desc: Variant of Amy, influenced by French Aimée.

name: Aimeric
desc: Probably a variant of Heimirich. Aimeric (or Aimery) was the name of several viscounts of Narbonne between the 11th and 13th centuries. It was also borne by the first king of Cyprus (12th century), originally from Poitou, France.

name: Aimery
desc: Old French form of Aimeric.

name: Aimi
desc: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" and 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other combinations of kanji characters are possible.

name: Aimilios
desc: Alternate transcription of Greek Αιμίλιος (see Emilios).

name: Aimo
desc: Means "generous amount" in Finnish.

name: Ain
desc: Possibly an Estonian short form of Hendrik.

name: Aina 1
desc: Variant of Aino. It also means "always" in Finnish.

name: Aina 2
desc: Balearic form of Anna.

name: Aina 3
desc: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" and 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", as well as other character combinations.

name: Aina 4
desc: Feminine form of Ainārs.

name: Aina 5
desc: Means "mirror" in Kazakh, ultimately from Persian آینه (ayneh).

name: Ainara
desc: Variant of Enara.

name: Ainārs
desc: From Latvian aina meaning "scene, sight".

name: Aindrea
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Andrew.

name: Aindréas
desc: Irish form of Andrew.

name: Aindriú
desc: Irish form of Andrew.

name: Áine
desc: Means "radiance, brilliance" in Irish. This was the name of a goddess of love and fertility in Irish legend, thought to dwell at the hill of Cnoc Áine in Limerick. It has sometimes been Anglicized as Anne.

name: Aineias
desc: Ancient Greek form of Aeneas.

name: Aingeal
desc: Irish cognate of Angela.

name: Aingeru
desc: Basque form of Angelus (see Angel).

name: Ainhoa
desc: From the name of a town in southwest France where there is a famous image of the Virgin Mary.

name: Aino
desc: Means "the only one" in Finnish. In the Finnish epic the Kalevala this is the name of a girl who drowns herself when she finds out she must marry the old man Väinämöinen.

name: Ainoa
desc: Spanish form of Ainhoa.

name: Ainslee
desc: Variant of Ainsley.

name: Ainsley
desc: From an English surname that was from a place name: either Annesley in Nottinghamshire or Ansley in Warwickshire. The place names themselves derive from Old English anne "alone, solitary" or ansetl "hermitage" and leah "woodland, clearing".... [more]

name: Ainslie
desc: Variant of Ainsley.

name: Aintza
desc: Means "glory" in Basque.

name: Aintzane
desc: Variant of Aintza.

name: Ainur
desc: Kazakh form of Aynur.

name: Ainura
desc: Kyrgyz form of Aynur.

name: Aiolos
desc: Means "quick-moving, nimble" in Greek. This was the name of the Greek god of the winds.

name: Aira
desc: Variant of Airi 2.

name: Airat
desc: Alternate transcription of Tatar/Bashkir Айрат (see Ayrat).

name: Airi 1
desc: From Japanese 愛 (ai) meaning "love, affection" combined with 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine" or 梨 (ri) meaning "pear". Other combinations of kanji characters are possible.

name: Airi 2
desc: From Finnish airut meaning "messenger, herald", also influenced by place names beginning with the same sound.

name: Airmanagild
desc: Gothic form of Hermenegildo.

name: Airmanareiks
desc: Gothic form of Ermenrich.

name: Aişə
desc: Azerbaijani form of Aisha.

name: Aischylos
desc: Greek form of Aeschylus.

name: 'Aisha
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عائشة (see Aisha).

name: A'isha
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عائشة (see Aisha).

name: Aisha
usage: Arabic, Urdu, Western African, Eastern African, Hausa, Swahili, Kazakh, African American
desc: Means "living, alive" in Arabic. This was the name of Muhammad's third wife, the daughter of Abu Bakr. Some time after Muhammad's death she went to war against Ali, the fourth caliph, but was defeated. Her name is used more by Sunni Muslims and less by Shias.... [more]

name: Aishah
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عائشة (see Aisha), as well as the usual Malay form.

name: Aishat
desc: Chechen form of Aisha.

name: Aishath
desc: Dhivehi form of Aisha.

name: Aishatu
desc: Hausa variant of Aisha.

name: Aishwarya
usage: Indian, Hindi, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil
desc: Means "prosperity, wealth" in Sanskrit. A famous bearer is the Indian actress Aishwarya Rai Bachchan (1973-).

name: Aislin
desc: Variant of Aisling.

name: Aisling
desc: Means "dream" or "vision" in Irish. This name was created in the 20th century.

name: Aislinn
desc: Variant of Aisling.

name: Aisopos
desc: Ancient Greek form of Aesop.

name: Aïssa
desc: Form of Aisha used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Aïssatou
desc: Form of Aisha used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Aistė
desc: From the name of the Baltic tribe of the Aesti, mentioned by the Roman historian Tacitus, called the Aisçiai in Lithuanian.

name: Aisultan
desc: Derived from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and сұлтан (sultan) meaning "sultan, king" (of Arabic origin).

name: Aisyah
desc: Indonesian form of Aisha.

name: Aitana
desc: From the name of a mountain range in Valencia, eastern Spain. The Spanish poet Rafael Alberti used it for his daughter in 1941.

name: Aithan
desc: Form of Ethan used in the Greek Old Testament.

name: Aithbhreac
desc: Older form of Oighrig. This name was borne by the 15th-century Scottish poet Aithbhreac Inghean Coirceadal.

name: Aither
desc: Greek form of Aether.

name: Aithne
desc: Possibly a variant of Eithne.

name: Aitor
desc: Possibly means "good fathers" from Basque aita "father" and on "good". This was the name of a legendary ancestor of the Basques.

name: Aivar
desc: Estonian form of Ivar.

name: Aivars
desc: Latvian form of Ivar. The Latvian author Vilis Lācis used it for a character in his novel Uz Jauno Krastu (1952).

name: Aiza
desc: Meaning unknown, possibly of Arabic origin.

name: Aizah
desc: Alternate transcription of Urdu عائزہ (see Aiza).

name: Aizere
desc: Means "golden moon" from Kazakh ай (ay) meaning "moon" and Persian زر (zar) meaning "gold".

name: Ajax
desc: From the Greek name Αἴας (Aias), perhaps deriving from Greek αἰαστής (aiastes) meaning "mourner" or αἶα (aia) meaning "earth, land". In Greek mythology this was the name of two of the heroes who fought for the Greeks in the Trojan War, the son of Telamon and the son of Oileus. When the armour of the slain hero Achilles was not given to Ajax Telamonian, he became mad with jealousy and killed himself.

name: Ajay
usage: Indian, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil
desc: Means "unconquered", from Sanskrit अ (a) meaning "not" and जय (jaya) meaning "victory, conquest".

name: Ajda 1
desc: Turkish form of Ayda.

name: Ajda 2
desc: Means "buckwheat" in Slovene.

name: Ajdin
desc: Bosnian form of Aydın.

name: Ajeet
desc: Alternate transcription of Hindi अजीत, Marathi अजित, Gurmukhi ਅਜੀਤ or Bengali অজিত (see Ajit).

name: Ajei
desc: From Navajo ajéí meaning "heart".

name: Ajit
desc: Means "unconquered, invincible", from Sanskrit अ (a) meaning "not" and जित (jita) meaning "conquered". This is a name of the gods Shiva and Vishnu, and of a future Buddha.

name: Ajith
desc: Southern Indian form of Ajit.

name: Ajla
desc: Bosnian and Albanian form of Ayla 2.

name: Ajna
desc: Bosnian form of Aina 5.

name: Ajnur
desc: Bosnian masculine form of Aynur.

name: Ajša
desc: Bosnian form of Aisha.

name: Akachi
desc: Means "the hand of God" in Igbo.

name: Akaki
desc: Georgian form of Akakios.

name: Akakios
desc: From a Greek word meaning "innocent, not evil", derived from ἀ (a), a negative prefix, combined with κάκη (kake) meaning "evil". This was the name of three early saints, two of whom were martyred.

name: Akamu
desc: Hawaiian form of Adam.

name: Akane
desc: From Japanese 茜 (akane) meaning "deep red, dye from the rubia plant". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

name: Akanksha
desc: Means "desire, wish" in Sanskrit.

name: Akantha
desc: Greek form of Acantha.

name: Akari
desc: From Japanese 明 (aka) meaning "bright" or 朱 (aka) meaning "vermilion red" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village" or 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

name: Akash
desc: Means "open space, sky" in Sanskrit.

name: Akbar
usage: Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Indonesian, Indian (Muslim)
desc: Means "greater, greatest" in Arabic. This was the name of a 16th-century Mughal ruler who expanded the empire to include most of India.

name: Åke
desc: Swedish form of Áki.

name: Akeem
desc: Perhaps a variant of Hakim.

name: Akemi
desc: From Japanese 明 (ake) meaning "bright" and 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

name: Akhenaten
desc: Variant of Akhenaton.

name: Akhenaton
desc: From Egyptian ꜣḫ-n-jtn meaning "effective for Aton". Akhenaton was a 14th-century BC Egyptian pharaoh of the New Kingdom, who is best known for promoting the monotheistic worship of the sun god Aton. He changed his name from Amenhotep in order to honour the god. After his death, polytheism resumed.

name: Akhil
desc: Means "whole, complete" in Sanskrit.

name: Akhila
desc: Feminine form of Akhil.

name: Akhmad
desc: Chechen, Ingush and Indonesian form of Ahmad.

name: Akhmat
desc: Bashkir and Tatar form of Ahmad.

name: Akhmet
desc: Kazakh form of Ahmad.

name: 'Akhsah
desc: Hebrew form of Achsah.

name: Áki
desc: Old Norse diminutive of names containing the element anu "ancestor".

name: Aki 1
desc: Short form of Joakim.

name: Aki 2
desc: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn". It can also come from 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" combined with 希 (ki) meaning "hope". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can form this name too.

name: Akiba
desc: Alternate transcription of Hebrew עֲקִיבָא (see Akiva).
