name: Akicita
desc: From Lakota or Dakota akíčhita meaning "warrior".

name: Akie
desc: From Japanese 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" or 昭 (aki) meaning "bright" combined with 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting" or 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

name: Akihiko
desc: From Japanese 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

name: Akihito
desc: From Japanese 明 (aki) or 昭 (aki) both meaning "bright" combined with 仁 (hito) meaning "compassionate". Other kanji combinations are possible. Akihito (1933-), name written 明仁, was the emperor of Japan from 1989 to 2019.

name: Akiko
desc: From Japanese 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other combinations of kanji characters are possible.

name: Akilah
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic عقيلة or عاقلة (see Aqila).

name: Akilina
desc: Russian form of the Roman name Aquilina, a feminine derivative of Aquila.

name: Akim
desc: Russian form of Joachim.

name: Akimitsu
desc: From Japanese 昭 (aki) meaning "bright" and 光 (mitsu) meaning "light". Other combinations of kanji can also form this name.

name: Akinyi
desc: Means "born in the morning" in Luo.

name: Akio
desc: From Japanese 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 男 (o) meaning "male, man" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

name: Akira
desc: From Japanese 昭 (akira) meaning "bright", 明 (akira) meaning "bright" or 亮 (akira) meaning "clear". Other kanji with the same pronunciation can also form this name. A famous bearer was the Japanese filmmaker Akira Kurosawa (1910-1998), given name written 明.

name: Akito
desc: From Japanese 章 (aki) meaning "chapter" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation, or 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

name: Akiva
desc: From an Aramaic form of Yaakov. Akiva (or Akiba) ben Joseph was a prominent 1st-century Jewish rabbi.

name: Akmad
desc: Maguindanao and Tausug form of Ahmad.

name: Akmal
desc: Means "more perfect, more complete" in Arabic, a comparative form of كامل (kamil).

name: Akmaral
desc: Derived from Kazakh ақ (aq) meaning "white" and марал (maral) meaning "deer".

name: Akmat
desc: Kyrgyz form of Ahmad.

name: Akoni
desc: Short form of Anakoni.

name: Ákos
desc: Possibly of Turkic origin meaning "white falcon". This was the name of a medieval Hungarian clan.

name: Akosua
desc: Means "born on Sunday" in Akan.

name: Akpan
desc: Means "first-born son" in Ibibio.

name: Akpofure
desc: Means "life is peaceful" in Urhobo.

name: Akram
desc: Means "most generous" in Arabic (a superlative form of Karim).

name: Aksana
desc: Belarusian form of Xenia.

name: Aksel
desc: Variant of Axel.

name: Akseli
desc: Finnish form of Axel.

name: Akshay
desc: Means "undecaying, imperishable" in Sanskrit.

name: Aksinia
desc: Bulgarian form of Xenia, as well as an alternate transcription of Russian Аксинья (see Aksinya).

name: Aksinya
desc: Variant of Kseniya.

name: Aku 1
desc: Short form of Aukusti.

name: Aku 2
desc: Ewe form of Akua.

name: Akua
desc: Means "born on Wednesday" in Akan.

name: Akuchi
desc: Means "wealth from God" in Igbo.

name: Akulina
desc: Variant of Akilina.

name: Akvilė
desc: Lithuanian feminine form of Aquila.

name: Al
desc: Short form of Albert and other names beginning with Al. A notable bearer is American actor Al Pacino (1940-).

name: Ala 1
desc: Means "excellence, elevation" in Arabic.

name: Ala 2
desc: Means "earth, land" in Igbo. In traditional Igbo religion Ala (called Ani or Ana in other dialects) is an earth goddess associated with fertility and ancestors.

name: Ala ad-Din
desc: Means "excellence of religion" from Arabic عَلَاء ('ala) meaning "excellence, elevation" combined with دين (din) meaning "religion, faith". This was the name of several sultans of Delhi.

name: Ala al-Din
desc: Alternate transcription of Arabic علاء الدين (see Ala ad-Din).

name: Alaattin
desc: Turkish form of Ala ad-Din.

name: Alaba
desc: Means "second child after twins" in Yoruba.

name: Aladdin
desc: Anglicized form of Ala ad-Din. This is the name of a mischievous boy in one of the tales of The 1001 Nights. A magician traps him in a cave, but he escapes with the help of a genie.

name: Alaia 1
desc: Means "joyful, happy" from Basque alai.

name: Alaia 2
desc: Probably a variant of Alayah. It is likely also influenced by the fashion brand Alaïa, named for the Tunisian-French designer Azzedine Alaïa (1935-2017). His surname in Arabic is عليّة ('Alayyah), meaning "lofty".

name: Alain
desc: French form of Alan.

name: Alaina
desc: Variant of Alana, probably influenced by Elaine.

name: Alaiya
desc: Variant of Alayah.

name: Alajos
desc: Hungarian form of Aloysius.

name: Al-Amir
desc: Means "the commander, the prince" in Arabic. This was the name of a 10th-century Fatimid imam.

name: Alan
desc: The meaning of this name is not known for certain. It was used in Brittany at least as early as the 6th century, and it possibly means either "little rock" or "handsome" in Breton. Alternatively, it may derive from the tribal name of the Alans, an Iranian people who migrated into Europe in the 4th and 5th centuries.... [more]

name: Alana
desc: Feminine form of Alan.

name: Alani
desc: Possibly a variant of Alana, or possibly from Hawaiian ʻalani meaning "orange (tree or fruit)".

name: Alanis
desc: Feminine form of Alan. Canadian musician Alanis Morissette (1974-) was named after her father Alan. Her parents apparently decided to use this particular spelling after seeing this word in a Greek newspaper.

name: Alanna
desc: Feminine form of Alan.

name: Alannah
desc: Variant of Alana. It has been influenced by the affectionate Anglo-Irish word alannah, from the Irish Gaelic phrase a leanbh meaning "O child".

name: Alannis
desc: Variant of Alanis.

name: Alaois
desc: Irish form of Aloysius.

name: Alard
desc: Variant of Adalhard.

name: Alareiks
desc: Gothic form of Alaric.

name: Alaric
desc: From the Gothic name *Alareiks meaning "ruler of all", derived from the element alls "all" combined with reiks "ruler, king". This was the name of a king of the Visigoths who sacked Rome in the 5th century.

name: Alasdair
desc: Scottish Gaelic form of Alexander.

name: Alassane
desc: Form of Al-Hasan used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

name: Alastair
desc: Anglicized form of Alasdair.

name: Alastar
desc: Irish form of Alexander.

name: Alastor
desc: Means "avenger" in Greek. This was an epithet of Zeus, as well as the name of several other characters from Greek mythology.

name: Alastríona
desc: Feminine form of Alastar.

name: Alawar
desc: Possible Frankish cognate of Álvaro.

name: Alaya
desc: Variant of Alayah. It coincides with a Buddhist term (meaning "dwelling" in Sanskrit), which refers to the eighth level of human consciousness.

name: Alayah
desc: Probably a variant of Aaliyah based on names such as Amaya and Anaya.

name: Alayna
desc: Variant of Alaina.

name: Alazne
desc: From Basque alatz meaning "miracle". It is an equivalent of Milagros, proposed by Sabino Arana in his 1910 list of Basque saints names.

name: Alba 1
desc: This name is derived from two distinct names, Alba 2 and Alba 3, with distinct origins, Latin and Germanic. Over time these names have become confused with one another. To further complicate the matter, alba means "dawn" in Italian, Spanish and Catalan. This may be the main inspiration behind its use in Italy and Spain.

name: Alba 2
desc: Feminine form of Albus.

name: Alba 3
desc: Originally a short form of Germanic names beginning with the element alb meaning "elf" (Proto-Germanic *albaz).

name: Albaer
desc: Limburgish form of Albert. Its spelling has been influenced by the French pronunciation of Albert.

name: Alban
desc: From the Roman cognomen Albanus, which meant "from Alba". Alba (from Latin albus "white") was the name of various places within the Roman Empire, including the city Alba Longa. This name was borne by Saint Alban, the first British martyr (4th century). According to tradition, he sheltered a fugitive priest in his house. When his house was searched, he disguised himself as the priest, was arrested in his stead, and was beheaded. Another 4th-century martyr by this name was Saint Alban of Mainz.... [more]

name: Albana
desc: Feminine form of Albanus (see Alban).

name: Albane
desc: French feminine form of Alban.

name: Albano
desc: Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of Albanus (see Alban).

name: Albanus
desc: Latin form of Alban.

name: Albarīks
desc: Proto-Germanic reconstruction of Alberich, Ælfric and Alfríkr.

name: Albaweniz
desc: Proto-Germanic reconstruction of Ælfwine, Alboin and Alfvin.

name: Albena
desc: Created by Bulgarian writer Yordan Yovkov for the heroine in his drama Albena (1930). He may have based it on ablen, the name of a type of peony (a flowering plant).

name: Alberic
desc: Variant of Alberich.

name: Alberich
desc: Derived from the Old German elements alb "elf" and rih "ruler, king". It was borne by two Lombard dukes of Spoleto in the 10th century. It was also the name of a 12th-century French saint who helped found the Cistercian Order.... [more]

name: Alberico
desc: Italian form of Alberich.

name: Albert
usage: English, German, French, Catalan, Polish, Czech, Russian, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Icelandic, Finnish, Romanian, Hungarian, Albanian, Germanic
desc: From the Germanic name Adalbert meaning "noble and bright", composed of the elements adal "noble" and beraht "bright". This name was common among medieval German royalty. The Normans introduced it to England, where it replaced the Old English cognate Æþelbeorht. Though it became rare in England by the 17th century, it was repopularized in the 19th century by the German-born Prince Albert, the husband of Queen Victoria.... [more]

name: Alberta
desc: Feminine form of Albert. This is the name of a Canadian province, which was named in honour of a daughter of Queen Victoria.

name: Albertas
desc: Lithuanian form of Albert.

name: Alberte 1
desc: Galician form of Albert.

name: Alberte 2
desc: French and Danish feminine form of Albert.

name: Albertina
desc: Feminine diminutive of Albert.

name: Albertine
desc: French feminine form of Albert.

name: Alberto
desc: Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Albert.

name: Alberts
desc: Latvian form of Albert.

name: Albertus
desc: Latinized form of Albert. This is the official Dutch form of the name, used on birth certificates but commonly rendered Albert in daily life.

name: Albie
desc: Diminutive of Albert.

name: Albin
desc: Form of Albinus in several languages.

name: Albína
desc: Czech and Slovak form of Albina.

name: Albina
usage: Russian, Ukrainian, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Slovene, Polish, German, Lithuanian, Belarusian, Ancient Roman
desc: Feminine form of Albinus. This was the name of a few early saints, including a 3rd-century martyr from Caesarea.

name: Albinas
desc: Lithuanian form of Albinus.

name: Albine
desc: French form of Albina.

name: Albino
desc: Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of Albinus.

name: Albinus
desc: Roman cognomen that was a derivative of Albus. Saint Albinus (also called Aubin) was a 6th-century bishop of Angers in Brittany.

name: Alboin
desc: From the Old German elements alb "elf" and wini "friend". It is a cognate of Ælfwine. This was the name of a 6th-century king of the Lombards who began the Lombard conquest of Italy.

name: Alborz
desc: From the name of a mountain range (of unknown etymology) in northern Iran.

name: Albrecht
desc: German variant of Albert.

name: Albus
desc: Roman cognomen meaning "white, bright" in Latin.

name: Alby
desc: Anglicized masculine form of Ailbhe.

name: Alcaeus
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀλκαῖος (Alkaios) meaning "strong", derived from ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess". This was the name of a 7th-century BC lyric poet from the island of Lesbos.

name: Alcestis
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἄλκηστις (Alkestis), derived from ἀλκηστής (alkestes) meaning "brave, valiant", a derivative of ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess". In Greek mythology she was the wife of King Admetus. She offered to die in place of her husband, though she was eventually rescued from the underworld by Herakles. This story was told by the Greek playwright Euripides in his 5th-century BC tragedy Alcestis.

name: Alcibiades
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀλκιβιάδης (Alkibiades), derived from ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess" and βία (bia) meaning "force" with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides). This was the name of a notable Greek statesman and general during the Peloponnesian War. He changed allegiance from Athens to Sparta and back again during the course of the war. He features in Shakespeare's tragedy Timon of Athens (1607).

name: Alcide
desc: Italian and French form of Alcides.

name: Alcides
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἀλκείδης (Alkeides), derived from ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess" and the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides). This was another name for the hero Herakles.

name: Alcippe
desc: From Greek Ἀλκίππη (Alkippe), derived from ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess" and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse". This was the name of a daughter of Ares in Greek myth. Her father killed Halirrhotis, a son of Poseidon, when he attempted to rape her, leading to a murder trial in which Ares was quickly acquitted.

name: Alcmene
desc: From Greek Ἀλκμήνη (Alkmene), derived from ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess" combined with μήνη (mene) meaning "moon" or μῆνις (menis) meaning "wrath". In Greek mythology Alcmene was the wife of Amphitryon. She was the mother of Herakles by Zeus, who bedded her by disguising himself as her absent husband.

name: Alcyone
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἀλκυόνη (Alkyone), derived from the word ἀλκυών (alkyon) meaning "kingfisher". In Greek myth this name belonged to a daughter of Aeolus and the wife of Ceyx. After her husband was killed in a shipwreck she threw herself into the water, but the gods saved her and turned them both into kingfishers. This is also the name of the brightest of the Pleiades, a group of stars in the constellation Taurus, supposedly the daughters of Atlas and Pleione.

name: Alda 1
desc: Feminine form of Aldo.

name: Alda 2
desc: Means "wave" in Icelandic.

name: Aldara
desc: Galician form of the Visigothic name *Hildiwara, which was composed of the Gothic elements hilds "battle" and wars "aware, cautious". This was the name of the 7th-century wife of the Visigothic king Gundemar. It was also borne by the mother of Saint Rosendo (10th century).

name: Aldebrand
desc: Old German name derived from the elements alt meaning "old" and brant meaning "fire, torch, sword". Saint Aldebrand was a 12th-century bishop of Fossombrone in Italy.

name: Aldegar
desc: Derived from the Old German elements alt "old" and ger "spear".

name: Aldegonda
desc: Dutch form of Aldegund.

name: Aldegund
desc: Germanic name, derived from the elements alt "old" and gunda "war". Alternatively, it could be a metathesized form of Adalgund. Saint Aldegund (or Aldegundis or Adelgundis) was a 7th-century Frankish abbess at Maubeuge.

name: Aldegundis
desc: Latinized form of Aldegund.

name: Alden
desc: From a surname that was derived from the Old English given name Ealdwine.

name: Aldéric
desc: Variant of Aldric.

name: Aldert
desc: Frisian form of a Germanic name, either Aldhard or Adalhard.

name: Aldhard
desc: Derived from the Old German elements alt "old" and hart "hard, firm, brave, hardy".

name: Aldin
desc: Bosnian form of Ala ad-Din.

name: Aldina 1
desc: Feminine form of Aldo.

name: Aldina 2
desc: Bosnian feminine form of Ala ad-Din.

name: Aldith
desc: Middle English form of Ealdgyð.

name: Aldiyar
desc: Derived from the archaic Kazakh title алдияр (aldiyar), which was used to address a ruler (equivalent to English Your Majesty). The word is ultimately of Persian origin, but of uncertain meaning.

name: Aldo
desc: Originally a short form of Germanic names beginning with the element alt meaning "old" (Proto-Germanic *aldaz), and sometimes also with adal meaning "noble" (Proto-Germanic *aþalaz).

name: Aldona
desc: Meaning unknown. This was the name of a 14th-century Polish queen, the daughter of a Grand Duke of Lithuania.

name: Aldous
desc: Probably a diminutive of names beginning with the Old English element eald "old". It has been in use as an English given name since the Middle Ages, mainly in East Anglia. The British author Aldous Huxley (1894-1963) was a famous bearer of this name.

name: Aldreda
desc: Variant of Etheldred.

name: Aldric
desc: From a Germanic name, derived from the elements alt "old" and rih "ruler, king". Saint Aldric was a 9th-century bishop of Le Mans.

name: Aldus
desc: Medieval variant of Aldous.

name: Aldwin
desc: Derived from the Old German elements alt "old" and wini "friend". This is a cognate of Old English Ealdwine.

name: Ale 1
desc: Finnish short form of Aleksanteri or Aleksi, an Italian short form of Alessandro, and a Spanish short form of Alejandro or Alejandra.

name: Ale 2
desc: Originally a short form of Germanic names beginning with the element adal meaning "noble".

name: Alea
desc: Variant of Aaliyah.

name: Aleah
desc: Variant of Aaliyah.

name: Alease
desc: Possibly a variant of Alicia.

name: Alec
desc: Short form of Alexander.

name: Alecia
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Aleĉjo
desc: Esperanto diminutive of Alexander.

name: Alecto
desc: Latinized form of Greek Ἀληκτώ (Alekto), which was derived from ἄληκτος (alektos) meaning "unceasing". This was the name of one of the Furies or Ἐρινύες (Erinyes) in Greek mythology.

name: Aled
desc: From the name of a Welsh river, of uncertain meaning.

name: Aleesha
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Aleh
desc: Belarusian form of Oleg.

name: Aleid
desc: Dutch short form of Adelaide.

name: Aleida
desc: Dutch short form of Adelaide.

name: Áleifr
desc: Old Norse form of Olaf.

name: Aleix
desc: Catalan form of Alexis.

name: Aleixo
desc: Portuguese and Galician form of Alexis.

name: Alejandra
desc: Spanish form of Alexandra.

name: Alejandro
desc: Spanish form of Alexander. This was the most popular name for boys in Spain from the 1990s until 2006 (and again in 2011).

name: Alejo
desc: Spanish form of Alexis.

name: Aleka
desc: Diminutive of Alexandra.

name: Alekos
desc: Diminutive of Alexandros.

name: Aleks
desc: Short form of Aleksey, Aleksandr or Aleksandra.

name: Aleksandar
desc: Form of Alexander in several languages.

name: Aleksandër
desc: Albanian form of Alexander.

name: Aleksander
desc: Form of Alexander in several languages.

name: Aleksandr
desc: Russian and Armenian form of Alexander. This name was borne by the 19th-century Russian poet Aleksandr Pushkin.

name: Aleksandra
usage: Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Serbian, Bulgarian, Slovene, Croatian, Macedonian, Finnish, Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Georgian
desc: Form of Alexandra in several languages.

name: Aleksandras
desc: Lithuanian form of Alexander.

name: Aleksandre
desc: Georgian form of Alexander.

name: Aleksandrina
desc: Diminutive of Aleksandra.

name: Aleksandro
desc: Esperanto form of Alexander.

name: Aleksandrs
desc: Latvian form of Alexander.

name: Aleksandru
desc: Old Slavic form of Alexander.

name: Aleksanteri
desc: Finnish form of Alexander.

name: Aleksei
desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Алексей (see Aleksey).

name: Aleksej
desc: Slovene form of Alexis.

name: Aleksejs
desc: Latvian form of Aleksey.

name: Aleksey
desc: Russian form of Alexis. This was the name of a 17th-century czar of Russia.

name: Aleksi
desc: Finnish, Bulgarian and Georgian form of Alexis.

name: Aleksy
desc: Polish form of Alexis.

name: Alekto
desc: Greek form of Alecto.

name: Alem

name: Alexander
usage: English, German, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Icelandic, Hungarian, Slovak, Biblical, Ancient Greek (Latinized), Greek Mythology (Latinized)
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀλέξανδρος (Alexandros), which meant "defending men" from Greek ἀλέξω (alexo) meaning "to defend, help" and ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man" (genitive ἀνδρός). In Greek mythology this was another name of the hero Paris, and it also belongs to several characters in the New Testament. However, the most famous bearer was Alexander the Great, king of Macedon. In the 4th century BC he built a huge empire out of Greece, Egypt, Persia, and parts of India. Due to his fame, and later medieval tales involving him, use of his name spread throughout Europe.... [more]

name: Alexandr
desc: Czech form of Alexander, as well as an alternate transcription of Russian Александр (see Aleksandr).

name: Alexandra
usage: English, German, Dutch, French, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Icelandic, Greek, Portuguese, Romanian, Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Catalan, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Ukrainian, Ancient Greek, Greek Mythology
desc: Feminine form of Alexander. In Greek mythology this was a Mycenaean epithet of the goddess Hera, and an alternate name of Cassandra. It was borne by several early Christian saints, and also by the wife of Nicholas II, the last czar of Russia. She was from Germany and had the birth name Alix, but was renamed Александра (Aleksandra) upon joining the Russian Church.

name: Alexandre
desc: Form of Alexander in several languages. This name was borne by the 19th-century French author Alexandre Dumas (1802-1870), who wrote The Three Musketeers.

name: Alexandrea
desc: Variant of Alexandria.

name: Alexandria
desc: Feminine form of Alexander. Alexander the Great founded several cities by this name (or renamed them) as he extended his empire eastward. The most notable of these is Alexandria in Egypt, founded by Alexander in 331 BC.

name: Alexandrie
desc: French variant of Alexandra.

name: Alexandrina
desc: Elaborated form of Alexandra. This was the first name of Queen Victoria; her middle name was Victoria.

name: Alexandrine
desc: French diminutive of Alexandra. This was the name of a Danish queen, the wife of King Christian X.

name: Alexandros
usage: Greek, Ancient Greek, Biblical Greek, Greek Mythology

name: Alexei

name: Alexey

name: Alexia

name: Alexina

name: Alexis
usage: French, English, Greek, Spanish, Ancient Greek
desc: From the Greek name Ἄλεξις (Alexis) meaning "helper" or "defender", derived from Greek ἀλέξω (alexo) meaning "to defend, to help". This was the name of a 3rd-century BC Greek comic poet, and also of several saints. It is used somewhat interchangeably with the related name Ἀλέξιος or Alexius, borne by five Byzantine emperors. In the English-speaking world it is more commonly used as a feminine name.

name: Alexius
desc: Latinized form of the Greek name Ἀλέξιος (Alexios), a derivative of Ἄλεξις (see Alexis). This was the name of five Byzantine emperors. It was also borne by a 5th-century Syrian saint who is especially venerated in the Eastern Church.

name: Alexsandr
desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Александр (see Aleksandr).

name: Alexus
desc: Variant of Alexis.

name: Aleyna
desc: From Arabic علينا ('alayna) meaning "on us", a word from the Quran.

name: Alf 1
desc: Derived from Old Norse alfr meaning "elf". In Norse legend this was the name of king, the suitor of a reluctant maiden named Alfhild. She avoided marrying him by disguising herself as a warrior, but when they fought she was so impressed by his strength that she changed her mind.

name: Alf 2
desc: Short form of Alfred.

name: Alf 3
desc: Short form of Adolf.

name: Alfarr
desc: Old Norse form of Alvar.

name: Alfbern
desc: Derived from the Old German elements alb "elf" and bern "bear".

name: Alfeo
desc: Italian form of Alphaeus.

name: Alfhard
desc: Old German name composed of the elements alb "elf" and hart "hard, firm, brave, hardy".

name: Alfher
desc: Old German name composed of the elements alb "elf" and heri "army" (making it a cognate of Alvar).

name: Alfhild
desc: From the Old Norse name Alfhildr, which was composed of the elements alfr "elf" and hildr "battle". In Scandinavian legend Alfhild was a maiden who disguised herself as a warrior in order to avoid marriage to King Alf. Her life was perhaps based on that of a 9th-century Viking pirate.

name: Alfhildr
desc: Old Norse form of Alfhild.

name: Alfia
desc: Possibly derived from Arabic ألْف (alf) meaning "thousand". Alternatively, it may be of Turkic origin.

name: Alfie
desc: Diminutive of Alfred.

name: Alfio
desc: Italian form of Alphius.

name: Alfiya
desc: Alternate transcription of Tatar Әлфия (see Alfia).

name: Alfons
desc: German, Dutch and Catalan form of Alfonso.

name: Alfonsas

name: Alfonsina
desc: Italian feminine form of Alfonso.

name: Alfonso
desc: Spanish and Italian form of Alphonsus, the Latin form of the Visigothic name *Aþalafuns meaning "noble and ready", derived from the Gothic elements aþals "noble" and funs "ready". This was the name of several kings of Spain (Asturias, León, Castile and Aragon) and Portugal, starting with Alfonso I of Asturias in the 8th century. His name was sometimes recorded in the Latin spelling Adefonsus, and on that basis it is theorized that first element might be from another source (perhaps haþus meaning "battle"). It is possible that two or more names merged into a single form.

name: Alfonz
desc: Slovak, Slovene and Hungarian form of Alfonso.

name: Alfr
desc: Old Norse form of Alf 1.

name: Alfréd
desc: Hungarian, Slovak and Czech form of Alfred.

name: Alfred
usage: English, French, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, German, Polish, Dutch, Albanian
desc: Means "elf counsel", derived from the Old English name Ælfræd, composed of the elements ælf "elf" and ræd "counsel, advice". Alfred the Great was a 9th-century king of Wessex who fought unceasingly against the Danes living in northeast England. He was also a scholar, and he translated many Latin books into Old English. His fame helped to ensure the usage of this name even after the Norman Conquest, when most Old English names were replaced by Norman ones. It became rare by the end of the Middle Ages, but was revived in the 18th century.... [more]

name: Alfvin
desc: From the Old Norse elements alfr "elf" and vinr "friend". It is a cognate of Ælfwine.

name: Alfwin
desc: Variant of Alboin.

name: Algar
desc: Means "elf spear" from Old English ælf "elf" and gar "spear". This Old English name was rarely used after the Norman Conquest, being absorbed by similar-sounding names and Norman and Scandinavian cognates. It was briefly revived in the 19th century.

name: Algautr
desc: From the Old Norse elements alfr meaning "elf" and gautr meaning "Geat" (a North Germanic tribe).

name: Alger
desc: From a surname that was derived from the given name Algar.

name: Algernon
desc: Originally a Norman French nickname, derived from aux gernons "having a moustache", which was applied to William de Percy, a companion of William the Conqueror. It was first used a given name in the 15th century (for a descendant of William de Percy). This name was borne by a character (a mouse) in the short story Flowers for Algernon (1958) and novel of the same title (1966) by the American author Daniel Keyes.

name: Algimantas
desc: From Lithuanian alga "salary, pay" combined with mantus "intelligent" or manta "property, wealth".

name: Algirdas
desc: Possibly means "all-hearing", from the Lithuanian roots al- "all, every" and gird- "to hear". This was the name of a 14th-century Grand Duke of Lithuania.

name: Algis
desc: Short form of Algimantas, Algirdas and other names beginning with the same sound.

name: Algot
desc: Swedish form of Algautr.

name: Alhaji
desc: Means "the pilgrim" in Hausa, a derivative of Arabic حَجّ (hajj) meaning "pilgrimage, hajj". It is typically a title, not a name.

name: Al-Hasan
desc: Form of Hasan prefixed with the Arabic definite article.

name: Alhassan
desc: Form of Al-Hasan used in western Africa.

name: Alheri
desc: Means "the charitable, the good" in Hausa, from Arabic خير (khayr).

desc: Means "lofty, sublime" in Arabic. Ali ibn Abi Talib was a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth caliph to rule the Muslim world. His followers were the original Shia Muslims, who regard him as the first rightful caliph.... [more]

name: Ali 2

name: Aliaksei

name: Alibrand
desc: From the Old German elements alles meaning "other, foreign" and brant meaning "fire, torch, sword".

name: Alica
desc: Slovak form of Alice.

name: Alice
usage: English, French, Portuguese, Italian, German, Czech, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Dutch
desc: From the Old French name Aalis, a short form of Adelais, itself a short form of the Germanic name Adalheidis (see Adelaide). This name became popular in France and England in the 12th century. It was among the most common names in England until the 16th century, when it began to decline. It was revived in the 19th century.... [more]

desc: Uyghur elaboration of Alim using the suffix جان (jan) meaning "dear, darling" (of Persian origin).

name: Alinafe
desc: Means "he or she is with us" in Chewa.

name: Aline
desc: Medieval short form of Adeline. As an English name, in modern times it has sometimes been regarded as a variant of Eileen. This was the name of a popular 1965 song by the French singer Christophe.

name: Alinur
desc: From the given name Ali 1 combined with Arabic نور (nur) meaning "light".

name: Aliona
desc: Alternate transcription of Russian Алёна or Ukrainian Альона (see Alyona).

name: Alireza
desc: Combination of Ali 1 and Reza, given in honour of the 9th-century Shia imam Ali ar-Ridha.

name: Alis

desc: From the given name Ali 1 combined with Persian شیر (sher) meaning "lion". It was borne by the 15th-century Timurid poet Ali-Shir Nava'i, who wrote in the Chagatai Turkic language.

name: Alishia
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Alisia
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Alison
desc: Norman French diminutive of Aalis (see Alice). It was common in England, Scotland and France in the Middle Ages, and was later revived in England in the 20th century via Scotland. Unlike most other English names ending in son, it is not derived from a surname.

name: Alissa
desc: Variant of Alyssa.

name: Alistair
desc: Anglicized form of Alasdair.

name: Alister
desc: Anglicized form of Alasdair.

name: Alisya
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Alita
desc: Possibly a variant of Alethea.

name: Alivia
desc: Variant of Olivia.

name: Alix
desc: Medieval French variant of Alice, also sometimes used as a masculine name. This is the name of the hero (a young Gaulish man) of a French comic book series, which debuted in 1948.

name: Aliya 1
desc: Kazakh and Tatar form of Aliyah 1, as well as an alternate transcription of Arabic عليّة (see Aliyah 1).

name: Aliya 2
desc: Means "ascent" in Hebrew, a derivative of עָלָה ('alah) meaning "to ascend, to climb". This is also a Hebrew word referring to immigration to Israel.

desc: Hungarian form of Alice.

desc: Means "joyful" in Hebrew.

name: Alizée
desc: From French alizé meaning "trade wind".

name: Alja
desc: Diminutive of Aleksandra.

name: Aljaž
desc: Derived from a Slovene surname, which is of unknown meaning.

name: Aljoša
desc: Slovene, Croatian and Serbian form of Alyosha. In Slovene it can also be a feminine name.

name: Alkaios
desc: Greek form of Alcaeus.

desc: Ancient Greek form of Alcyone.

name: Alla
desc: Meaning unknown, possibly of German origin.

name: Allah
desc: Derived from Arabic الإله (al-ilah) meaning "the deity". It is primarily used to refer to the Islamic God, though it was originally used by pre-Islamic Arabs, and is sometimes used by Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews.

name: Allan
desc: Variant of Alan. The American author Edgar Allan Poe (1809-1849) got his middle name from the surname of the parents who adopted him.

name: Allana
desc: Variant of Alana.

name: Allannah
desc: Variant of Alannah.

desc: Dutch form of Adalhard.

name: Alle
desc: Variant of Ale 2.

name: Allegra
desc: Means "cheerful, lively" in Italian. It was borne by a short-lived illegitimate daughter of Lord Byron (1817-1822).

name: Allegria
desc: Means "cheerfulness, joy" in Italian.

name: Allen
desc: Variant of Alan, or from a surname that was derived from this same name. A famous bearer of this name was Allen Ginsberg (1926-1997), an American beat poet. Another is the American film director and actor Woody Allen (1935-), who took the stage name Allen from his real first name.

name: Alli
desc: Finnish diminutive of names beginning with Al. This is also the Finnish word for a type of duck.

name: Allie
desc: Diminutive of Alison, Alexandra and other names beginning with the same sound. After a 34-year absence from the American top 1000 chart this name began growing in popularity after the premiere of the sitcom Kate and Allie in 1984.

name: Allison
desc: From the middle of the 20th century this has primarily been used as a variant of the feminine name Alison. However, prior to that it was used as an uncommon masculine name, derived from the English and Scottish surname Allison.

name: Allissa
desc: Variant of Alyssa.

name: Allochka
desc: Russian diminutive of Alla.

name: Allon
desc: Means "oak" in Hebrew. This name is mentioned briefly in the Old Testament.

name: Ally 1
desc: Diminutive of Alison, Alexandra and other names beginning with the same sound. This name jumped in popularity in 1997 after the premiere of the American television series Ally McBeal.

name: Ally 2
desc: Diminutive of Alistair.

name: Allycia
desc: Variant of Alicia.

name: Allyn
desc: Variant or feminine form of Alan.

name: Allyson
desc: Variant of Alison.

name: Alma 1
usage: English, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, German, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish, Latvian, Lithuanian, Albanian, Slovene, Croatian
desc: This name became popular after the Battle of Alma (1854), which took place near the River Alma in Crimea and ended in a victory for Britain and France. However, the name was in rare use before the battle; it was probably inspired by Latin almus "nourishing". It also coincides with the Spanish word meaning "the soul".

name: Alma 2
desc: Means "young woman" in Hebrew.

name: Alma 3
desc: Meaning unknown. According to the Book of Mormon, this was the name of two prophets, father and son. Alma the Elder was a corrupt priest who repented after meeting the prophet Abinadi. Alma the Younger rebelled against the church, but repented and become a missionary and prophet.

name: Almantas
desc: From the Lithuanian root al- "all, every" combined with mantus "intelligent" or manta "property, wealth".

name: Almas
desc: Means "diamond" in Arabic, ultimately from Persian الماس (almas).

name: Almast
desc: Means "diamond" in Armenian, ultimately from Persian الماس (almas).

name: Almazbek
desc: From Kyrgyz алмаз (almaz) meaning "diamond", ultimately from Persian الماس (almas), combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

name: Almir 1
desc: Brazilian variant of Almiro.

name: Almir 2
desc: Bosnian form of Al-Amir.

name: Almira 1
desc: Variant of Elmira 1. Handel used it for the title character in his opera Almira (1705).

name: Almira 2
desc: Bosnian feminine form of Al-Amir.

name: Almiro
desc: Meaning uncertain, possibly a masculine form of Almira 1.

name: Almog
desc: Means "coral" in Hebrew.

name: Álmos
desc: Possibly from Hungarian álom "dream", though perhaps of Turkic origin meaning "bought". This was the name of the semi-legendary father of Árpád, the founder of the Hungarian state. Álmos's mother Emese supposedly had a dream in which a turul bird impregnated her and foretold that her son would be the father of a great nation.

name: Almudena
desc: Derived from Arabic المدينة (al-mudaynah) meaning "the citadel". It was in a building by this name that a concealed statue of the Virgin Mary was discovered during the Reconquista in Madrid. The Virgin of Almudena, that is Mary, is the patron saint of Madrid.

name: Alodia
desc: Possibly from a Visigothic name, maybe from Gothic elements such as alls "all" or aljis "other" combined with auds "riches, wealth". Saint Alodia was a 9th-century Spanish martyr with her sister Nunilo.

name: Álǫf
desc: Feminine form of Áleifr.

name: Alois
desc: German and Czech form of Aloysius.

name: Aloisia
desc: German feminine form of Aloysius.

name: Aloísio
desc: Portuguese form of Aloysius.

name: Aloisio
desc: Italian form of Aloysius.

desc: Slovak feminine form of Aloysius.

desc: Slovene and Croatian feminine form of Aloysius.

name: Alojzije
desc: Croatian form of Aloysius.

name: Alojzy
desc: Polish form of Aloysius.

name: Alon 1
desc: Means "oak tree" in Hebrew.

name: Alon 2

name: Alona
desc: Feminine form of Alon 1.

name: Alondra
desc: Derived from Spanish alondra meaning "lark".

name: Alonso
desc: Spanish variant of Alfonso.

name: Alonzo
desc: Variant of Alonso in use in America.

name: Alora
desc: Variant of Elora.

name: Aloys
desc: Medieval Occitan form of Louis.

name: Aloysia
desc: German feminine form of Aloysius.

name: Aloysius
desc: Latinized form of Aloys, an old Occitan form of Louis. This was the name of a 16th-century Italian saint, Aloysius Gonzaga. The name has been in occasional use among Catholics since his time.

name: Alp
desc: Means "hero" in Turkish.

name: Alparslan
desc: From Turkish alp meaning "brave" and arslan meaning "lion", referring to the 11th-century Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan, who expanded the Seljuk Empire into Anatolia.

name: Alpaslan
desc: Variant of Alparslan.

name: Alperen
desc: From Turkish alp "hero" and eren "holy person".

name: Alpertti
desc: Finnish form of Albert.

name: Alpha
desc: From the name of the first letter in the Greek alphabet, Α.

name: Alphaeus
desc: From Ἀλφαῖος (Alphaios), the Greek form of a Hebrew name that meant "changing". In the New Testament this is the name of the fathers of the apostles James and Levi.

name: Alphaios
desc: Greek form of Alphaeus.

name: Alphege
desc: Middle English form of Ælfheah.

name: Alphius
desc: Meaning unknown, possibly a variant of Alphaeus, or possibly from an Umbrian root meaning "white". This was the name of a 3rd-century saint who was martyred in Sicily.

name: Alphonse
desc: French form of Alfonso.

name: Alphonsine
desc: French feminine diminutive of Alfonso.

name: Alphonso
desc: Variant of Alfonso.

name: Alphonsus
desc: Latinized form of the Gothic name *Aþalfuns (see Alfonso). This name was borne by Saint Alphonsus Liguori, an 18th-century Italian bishop who is regarded as a Doctor of the Church.

name: Alphonzo
desc: Uncommon variant of Alfonso.

name: Alpin
desc: Anglicized form of the Scottish Gaelic name Ailpean, possibly derived from a Pictish word meaning "white". This was the name of two kings of Dál Riata and two kings of the Picts in the 8th and 9th centuries.

name: Alsu
desc: Means "pink" in Tatar.

name: Alta
desc: Possibly from Latin altus or Italian/Spanish alto meaning "high".

name: Altagracia
desc: Means "high grace", taken from the Spanish title of the Virgin Mary Nuestra Señora de la Altagracia, meaning "Our Lady of High Grace". She is considered the patron saint of the Dominican Republic, and it is there that this name is most often used.

name: Altair
desc: Means "the flyer" in Arabic. This is the name of a star in the constellation Aquila.

name: Altan 1
desc: Means "red dawn" in Turkish.

name: Altan 2
desc: Means "golden" in Mongolian.
